The Video Systems Specialist is a hands-on technical role supporting the delivery of premium live and broadcast experiences for Apple at Worldwide Events venues and remote locations. Acting as the team’s visual and display technical specialist, this role owns the end-to-end visual integrity, color fidelity, signal processing, and reliable operation of large- and small-format LED systems and video playback pipelines across rehearsals, live events, and broadcast productions.
The Video Systems Specialist collaborates across technical teams, producers, creative partners, and external vendors within Worldwide Events. Success in this role requires a sharp visual eye, deep technical rigor in display science and signal flow, and calm, precise execution in high-stakes, executive-facing environments with zero margin for error.
Minimum qualifications: 3+ years of hands-on technical experience with professional LED display systems, video processors, and live event video pipelines.
Demonstrated understanding of color science, color spaces (Rec.709, DCI-P3, Rec.2020), bit depth, dynamic range, and video inspection in tools like DaVinci Resolve.
Working knowledge of professional LED processing platforms (e.g., Megapixel Helios, Brompton Tessera).
Solid grasp of video engineering fundamentals: signal flow (SDI, HDMI, fiber, SMPTE 2110), EDID, aspect ratios, pixel mapping, raster management, genlock, and frame-rates.
Direct experience operating Apple Keynote and playback hardware in a technical production environment.
Experience with live event media servers and screen management switchers (e.g., Barco E2/E3, Disguise, Pixera).
Proven ability to communicate visual and technical issues cross-functionally with creative, editorial, and executive-facing teams under pressure.
Preferred qualifications: Broadcast and on-camera LED display experience, including shutter angle synchronization, refresh rates, scan lines, and camera-to-display moiré mitigation.
Experience with live event media servers and screen management switchers (e.g., Disguise, Pixera
Background supporting high-profile keynote presentations, premium product launches, or studio broadcast environments.

All of this is driven by a world-class vertically integrated engineering team spanning RF/Analog architecture and design, Systems/PHY/MAC architecture and design, VLSI/RTL design and integration, Emulation, Design Verification, Test and Validation, and FW/SW engineering.
In this role, and as part of our team, you will deliver an RF integration end-to-end Solution, which includes DUT control development, pre-silicon emulation/simulation, integrated RF calibration. You will become a central hub which enables different phases from design development toward Apple product’s mass production. You will also be responsible for Wireless SoC-RF Bring up at the first touch, final Silicon validation results and compliance. You will get the opportunity to keep developing your technical depth in both HW and SW domains, such as understanding of wireless transceiver architecture, RF system and DSP knowledge, Software framework, RF driver and embedded system, and experience of delivery Apple products until productization.
Minimum qualifications: Minimum requirement of a bachelors degree
Solid experience of RF parametric testing, such as IP3, NF, ACPR, phase noise, load pull.
Strong working knowledge of RF test equipments, such as; network analyzer, spectrum analyzer, vector signal analyzer, vector signal generator.
Strong Wireless RF background and familiarity with RF systems fundamentals, RF transceiver architectures and/or digital communication.
Preferred qualifications: Proficiency with understanding RFIC block-level design schematics.
Some experience of RF PCB board design, debug, and development.
Python programming language is highly desired.
Experience with embedded system and C programming language.
Automation framework development.

title: Wireless Systems Engineer
description:
Do you have a passion for wireless technologies? Do you want to impact the wireless experience for billions of users? Come and join us! You will become part of a hands-on development team that furthers engineering perfection, creativity, and innovation with a prime focus on wireless accuracy and performance. Dynamic, encouraging people and innovative technologies are the norm here. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish!
Join Apple’s System RF organization and drive innovation that matters! We’re looking for engineers who will re-imagine the way wireless performance of a device is analyzed and work cross-functionally with teams to deliver the best in class wireless performance for our customers. Our engineers help architect, research, and design, Apple’s world-class wireless products. All members of the numerous teams within the organization bring their own unique expertise to collectively bring wireless technologies to our products, following Apple’s culture of excellence in engineering principles and practices.
The job role will entail wireless performance research focused primarily on understanding how various factors like antenna performance, modem performance, SAR, RF algorithms, user interaction with device, channel conditions, co-ex and interference will impact wireless performance and in turn the end user experience. You will use these findings to work with cross-functional teams to help drive antenna, wireless algorithms and system level design and architecture changes.
Minimum qualifications: Masters degree in Electrical or Telecommunications Engineering or equivalent.
Strong understanding of cellular, WiFi or GNSS technologies.
Test automation experience. Python preferred and fluency with AI tools.
Preferred qualifications: 3+ years industry experience in RF and/or wireless systems.
Experience working on physical layer wireless algorithms.
Strong background in wireless communications.
Capturing and analyzing baseband logs to root cause performance issues.

title: Wireless Systems Engineer
description:
At Apple, you will have a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to deliver outstanding performance for wireless products. As a member of the Product RF Design team, you will be at the forefront of wireless technology as we push the boundaries of achievable performance in wireless for innovative products. You will become part of a hands-on product development team that shapes and influences current and future generations of Apple products. We’re looking for dedicated and motivated engineers with good fundamentals in one or more areas of RF/wireless and electromagnetic theory, antenna design, system integration, & wireless communications.
Product RF Design Engineers should have a broad-based knowledge in RF architecture, design, integration and manufacturing. They have deep theoretical and practical knowledge in one or more areas of electromagnetic theory, RF and Wireless circuit design, communication theory, and product design trade-off. They use electromagnetic and system simulation, hands on prototyping, test and measurement to understand complex system and sub-system interactions, implications to product level design, and manufacturing trade-offs to enable mass production.
Product RF Design Engineers apply their expertise in all aspects of product design from concept, architecture definition, integration and prototyping to final production. They work closely with wireless and software architects, industrial designers, and product designers to guide and sculpt the product design with an eye towards optimizing RF/Wireless functionality for the user. They work closely with manufacturing teams to support builds from prototype phase to mass production.
Minimum qualifications: BSEE or Equivalent education.
Coursework or experience in antenna/RF design, wireless communications, EM, or circuits.
Experience in antenna design including simulation, mockup skill and architecture investigation.
Experience in RF measurement and desense.
Preferred qualifications: Experience in integration of wireless technologies such as cellular, GPS, Wifi, and NFC into products.
Experience in RF schematic and PCB layout practices and guidelines.
Hands-on experience with RF lab instrumentation.
Ability to debug desense issues and characterize noise sources.
Experience with production environment and statistical analysis.
Excellent interpersonal skills, with ability to communicate effectively across cultures and geographical locations.
Strong collaborator, with ability to build strong relationships both within and outside the team.

title: Market Analyst
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns a fleet of distributed batteries and the households we serve into a power business that makes money. As a Market Analyst, you’ll know how much Base is earning, where it could lose money, and how it will make money in the next market.

You’ll own P&L (profit and loss) reporting and risk tracking across our battery fleet and retail operations. You’ll build the pricing models behind what we charge members, recommend hedges, and work with Finance, Growth and Legal & Policy to figure out how Base makes money in each new market. Base already does this in ERCOT. Your first job is to do it in PJM.

This role suits someone with a few years of experience in power markets, retail energy, or a related analytical field. You’ll own real decisions early.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build a bottoms-up retail pricing model for PJM that builds upon our ERCOT model.

 - Bring PJM into our risk system and P&L reporting, so we know the margin we earn and how to buy supply.

 - Identify new market opportunities and work closely with stakeholders from Finance, Growth and Legal & Policy teams to bring them to reality.

 - Recommend changes to Base’s hedging strategy in ERCOT and PJM, and track our exposure against risk limits.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Energy markets knowledge: you understand wholesale market basics in ERCOT and PJM, including how power is bought, hedged and settled. You know how retail pricing and operations work.

 - Commercial sense: you understand how a retail offer makes or loses money. You can explain the cost to supply it, the margin on it, and the risk in between.

 - Risk and statistics: you think in distributions, not point forecasts. You know power prices are tail heavy. Basic statistics is enough.

 - Coding and SQL: you build reports and models in Python (or another language), pull your own data with SQL, and work through a problem independently.

Nice to have: experience at a retail energy provider, utility supply desk, or trading middle office.



ABOUT THE TEAM

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns the grid-service capability of our distributed battery fleet into revenue. That means building and defending the models that decide which markets and products Base participates in, from real-time arbitrage to multi-year distribution deals. The team’s calls carry real weight - a mis-modeled coincident peak or an unvetted market opinion shows up directly in Base’s book. You’ll work alongside traders, market operations engineers, and policy leads who bring the same rigor to distribution-scale energy that a trading desk brings to wholesale power.

Job Description:
What It Means to Be a Consultant at Crowe
Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. In this role, you will continuously learn, collaborate across teams, and explore how tools, including emerging AI capabilities, can improve efficiency, insights, and client outcomes.
In management at Crowe, you play a pivotal role in leading teams, guiding project execution, and deepening client relationships. You are expected to contribute to account planning, identify opportunities to add value, and ensure high-quality delivery. As your responsibilities expand, you take on broader account ownership, balancing project leadership with growing involvement in client strategy and solution development.
Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence.
About the Role
Join our Financial Services Consulting practice and help organizations strengthen governance, manage risk, enhance internal controls, and navigate an increasingly complex regulatory environment.
As an Internal Audit Manager , you’ll work with banking and financial services clients on meaningful, high-impact engagements spanning internal audit, risk management, internal controls, and compliance. You’ll have the opportunity to lead client engagements, develop and mentor team members, build trusted relationships with client leaders, and recommend practical solutions that improve how organizations manage risk.
This role is ideal for an experienced internal audit professional who enjoys solving complex problems, leading teams, and working directly with clients in an entrepreneurial and collaborative consulting environment.
What You’ll Do
Lead and deliver internal audit, risk management, and internal control engagements for banking and financial services clients.
Plan engagements and manage project teams, including reviewing workpapers and providing coaching, feedback, and guidance to team members.
Conduct and oversee fieldwork, evaluate processes and controls, and develop well-supported conclusions and recommendations.
Communicate findings and observations to client management and prepare clear, actionable reports and presentations.
Advise clients on opportunities to strengthen and optimize internal controls and risk management practices.
Help clients enhance and transform internal audit approaches, methodologies, and operating models.
Perform risk assessments and identify opportunities to improve governance, processes, controls, and compliance.
Manage multiple projects and workstreams while maintaining strong client service and quality standards.
Manage engagement scope, staffing, workplans, budgets, schedules, billing, and overall engagement economics to deliver high-quality work on time and on budget.
Build trusted client relationships and contribute ideas that create additional value for clients and the firm.
Develop and expand relationships with client executives, identify emerging needs, and lead or contribute to proposals, scoping, presentations, and other sales-pursuit activities.
Coach and develop professionals through timely feedback, performance guidance, and career-development support, while holding project teams accountable for their commitments.
Contribute to market and practice growth through thought leadership, professional associations, recruiting, knowledge sharing, and development of new or improved service offerings.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree.
Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) or Certified Public Accountant (CPA) certification
5+ years of relevant experience in internal audit, internal controls assessment, and/or SOX 404 evaluation and testing, with experience serving organizations in the banking or financial services industry.
Experience managing projects and multiple concurrent workstreams and responsibilities.
Experience supervising, coaching, and reviewing the work of other professionals.
Strong understanding of internal control design and operating effectiveness.
Experience evaluating business processes, process flows, and flowcharts.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with clients and internal teams through interviews, meetings, presentations, reports, process narratives, and other formats.
Strong relationship-building and stakeholder-management skills.
Ability and willingness to travel as needed based on client and engagement requirements.
Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, or a Business or Economics degree with an Accounting minor or concentration.
Consulting or professional services experience supporting banking and financial services organizations.
Knowledge of GAAP financial accounting and SEC reporting requirements.
Experience advising organizations on internal audit transformation, risk assessments, internal controls optimization, or related risk and governance initiatives.
Demonstrated ability to develop client relationships, identify opportunities for improvement, and provide practical, value-added recommendations.
Experience operating in a collaborative, fast-paced environment where initiative, sound judgment, and effective project leadership are essential.

description:
About the Team
The Global Safety and Security team advances DoorDash through the protection of people, property, operations, brand, and reputation. We deliver value through agility, technology, and a people-first mindset—creating environments where employees and guests feel safe, welcome, and confident.
As DoorDash continues to evolve its workplace experience globally, our Corporate Safety and Security team is reimagining how physical security integrates seamlessly into every employee and guest interaction. The Associate, GOC Analyst will play a key role in designing and delivering this next-generation security experience.
About the Role
We are hiring a GOC Analyst to support DoorDash’s 24/7 Global Operations Center. Reporting to the GOC Manager, this role is responsible for real-time monitoring, incident triage, and operational response to protect DoorDash’s people, assets, and operations. As a frontline operator, you will serve as the first line of defense during emerging incidents—monitoring systems, assessing risk, executing SOPs, and escalating issues quickly and accurately. In addition to core operational response, you will apply foundational analytical skills to validate information, distinguish signal from noise, provide clear operational context that supports timely escalation and informed decision-making. You’ll operate in a high-tempo, follow-the-sun environment where clarity, discipline, and sound judgment are critical to maintaining operational resilience.
You are excited about this opportunity because you will…
Operate the GOC in Real Time: Monitor dashboards, alerts, inbound reports, and open-source signals to identify security, safety, and operational incidents as they emerge.

Maintain Situational Awareness: Track ongoing incidents, relevant global events, and operational conditions to maintain a clear, real-time understanding of risk across shifts and regions.
Apply Foundational Analytical  Tradecraft: Conduct initial fact-finding, source validation, and contextual analysis to distinguish signal from noise and support effective escalation.
Support Escalation and Decision-Making: Identify when issues exceed defined thresholds and escalate to the GOC Manager or Risk Intelligence team with clear, structured, and decision-ready information, without owning strategic risk interpretation.
Ensure Seamless Shift Handover: Produce concise shift reports and conduct disciplined handovers that capture incident status, risk context, and outstanding actions.
Contribute to Operational Excellence: Participate in drills, retrospectives, and continuous improvement efforts to strengthen GOC readiness, workflows, and analytical rigor.
Operate Calmly Under Pressure: Demonstrate professionalism, composure, and sound judgment during fast-moving or high-impact incidents.

Operations Center Experience: 3+ years in a GSOC, GOC, SOC, or comparable 24/7 operations or incident response environment.
Incident Management Fundamentals: Working knowledge of incident triage, escalation protocols, and operational playbooks.
Foundational Analytical Skills: Ability to assess information quality, identify trends or anomalies, and provide clear operational context during incidents.

Strong Operational Judgment: Ability to assess risk, prioritize tasks, and act decisively under pressure.
Technical Fluency: Comfort working across monitoring dashboards, ticketing systems, communication platforms, and basic analytics tools.
Clear Communication Skills: Ability to document incidents clearly and communicate effectively with leaders and cross-functional partners.

description:

About the Role
We’re looking for an Associate Manager to lead Consumer Growth GTM strategy for New Verticals. This person will shape how we bring priority merchants, categories, and customer behaviors to market, with a focus on bringing structure to a high volume of GTM opportunities and helping teams prioritize and execute them efficiently.
You will own the business strategy behind major growth moments: defining the customer opportunity, sizing the potential, recommending where to invest, setting goals, and translating insights into clear GTM plans. You will work closely with Marketing, Product, Analytics, Finance, and Business Development to ensure our plans are both strategically sound and operationally executable.
This is a highly visible role for someone who is equally comfortable digging into data, developing a point of view, and driving alignment across senior cross-functional stakeholders. We’re excited about you because you have…
4+ years of experience in strategy, operations, consulting, growth, business operations, product strategy, investment banking, or a related analytical and cross-functional environment.

A completed Bachelor’s degree.

title: Drone Operations, Intern - Labs (Summer 2027)
description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. The Drone Operations team keeps DoorDash's drones airworthy and operates them safely. Our missions range from experimental test flights to commercial delivery. We're hiring Drone Operations interns to work at the intersection of operations and robotics to solve key business problems with elegant technical solutions. If you have a passion for applying robotics solutions to a service loved by millions of people, then we want to talk to you!
About the Role
As a Drone Operations Intern, you will support daily flight operations for DoorDash’s drone delivery program, from our test flight program to our commercial operation. You will get exposure to all elements of our operation, including Pilots, Maintenance Technicians, Quality/Safety, and Engineering. title: Engineering Manager, Personalization
description:
About the Team
DoorDash is looking for an Engineering Manager with an ML background to lead the Personalization engineering team. This team is responsible for building ML ranking and recommendation systems to maximize the value for consumers, merchants, and DoorDash.
Our Personalization team is a part of our Core Consumer org which owns the top of the conversion funnel from the initial landing page all the way to checkout across platforms. Personalization is at the center of the team’s mission. As DoorDash expands into new verticals and experiences like grocery, reservations, and going out, the challenge of helping consumers easily find what they want grows exponentially, so the opportunity is massive!
In 2027, we’re reimagining personalization from the ground up: an intent agent that predicts, at app open, what each consumer is here for; semantic understanding of every entity we rank; a blender that blends content from different verticals and business lines, like reservations, going out, and ads; and real-time ranking that adapts as consumer signals happen.
About the Role
You will lead a team of world-class ML engineers redefining the personalization experience for DoorDash through cutting-edge technologies. You will also be the key player in defining DoorDash’s personalization strategy and technology roadmap.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Build an intent agent that makes granular predictions of what each consumer is here for the moment they open the app, and shapes the experience around it
Leverage cutting-edge LLM and Deep Learning (GNN, MTL, Transformers) to augment DoorDash’s personalization stack, starting with semantic understanding of every entity we rank, so our models understand what consumers want and what we offer, not just what they clicked before
Extend the blender to blend content from different verticals and business lines, like reservations, going out, and ads, balancing value for consumers, merchants, and DoorDash
Take personalization to real-time ranking that reacts to consumer signals as they happen
Lead and grow a team of exceptional machine learning engineers delivering on end-to-end personalization experience with state-of-the-art ML approaches
Work with Product, Design, and Business stakeholders directly across DoorDash to define the roadmap and vision for the team and deliver immense impact
Encourage innovation, implementation of cutting-edge technologies, outside-of-the-box thinking and teamwork
Build an outstanding team by coaching and empowering engineers through delegation, and applying your technical expertise to hold your team to the highest engineering standards
Scale the team by developing internal talent and attracting top external talent
We're excited about you because you have…
B.S., M.S., or PhD. in Computer Science or equivalent
7+ years of industry experience
Minimum of 2 years of leadership experience
Broad knowledge of machine learning with strong ML modeling foundation
Extensive experience in building user-facing product and working directly with product managers
Strong communication skills and the ability to partner with teams spanning many disciplines
Ability to guide and grow an excellent engineering team in a rapidly changing business environment
Nice to have
Experience leading the successful application of machine learning to real-world ranking and recommendation problems
Experience with LLM-powered agents, semantic representations of users and content, multi-objective blending, or real-time ML systems

title: Mechanical Engineer - Engineer, Chassis & Vehicle Dynamic
description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike.  We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact.  We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries.  As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries.  We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better
About the Role
We’re looking for a Mechanical Engineer to develop and improve chassis systems and vehicle dynamics performance for DOT, DoorDash’s autonomous delivery robot. You’ll combine hands-on mechanical design, engineering analysis, and vehicle testing to improve existing platforms and develop suspension and chassis solutions for future projects.
You’ll own engineering work from requirements and concept development through detailed CAD design, prototype evaluation, and validation. Working closely with internal teams and suppliers, you’ll assess designs, resolve technical challenges, and ensure chassis systems meet our performance, durability, and integration requirements.
This role offers the opportunity to influence how DOT rides, handles, brakes, and traverses real-world terrain while improving the reliability and serviceability of our deployed robots.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Design and improve suspension and chassis systems , including suspension geometry, linkages, wheel-end assemblies, and drivetrain and brake mounting interfaces.
Own mechanical design execution , developing concepts, detailed CAD models, engineering drawings, GD&T, and tolerance analyses to support prototype builds and production release.
Sustain and improve existing platforms , investigating field issues, performing root cause analysis, and implementing validated engineering changes.
Define chassis and vehicle dynamics requirements for ride quality, traction, braking, stability, ground clearance, and obstacle traversal across terrain and payload conditions.
Provide technical oversight of supplier-developed hardware , reviewing designs, analyses, and test results to ensure systems meet vehicle requirements and integrate successfully.
Develop and execute verification and validation plans with reliability, test, and integration teams, establishing measurable acceptance criteria for components and complete vehicles.
Lead instrumented vehicle dynamics testing , analyze results, and translate findings into hardware improvements and operating limits.
Partner with controls and autonomy engineers to characterize vehicle capabilities and improve motion performance.
Support prototype builds, manufacturing, and service teams , resolving integration issues and improving durability, manufacturability, and maintainability .
We’re excited about you because…
You have a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field.
You have experience designing and developing suspension, chassis, or related mechanical systems for vehicles or mobile robots.
You understand suspension kinematics, load transfer, tire behavior, stiffness and damping, braking, and vehicle stability—and can apply these fundamentals to hardware design.
You are proficient in NX, SolidWorks, CATIA, or a comparable CAD platform and have experience releasing detailed mechanical designs.
You apply sound engineering judgment to load cases, structural integrity, fatigue, bearings, bolted joints, materials, and manufacturing processes.

title: Senior Manager, Protective Services
description:
About the Team
DoorDash is one of the world's most trusted on-demand logistics platforms. The Global Safety and Security team exists to keep it that way, protecting our people, property, operations, brand, and reputation across all our markets. We manage risk and create value through agility, technology, and a people-first approach. Our DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt brands now span more than 40 countries, dozens of offices, and tens of thousands of employees. Protective Services is the function accountable for the safety of the people we protect and the environments they live and work in, wherever they are.
About the Role
We are hiring a Senior Manager, Protective Services to lead protective operations, reporting to the Director, Protective Services. This is as much a build-and-execute mandate as a leadership one. You own the decisions that keep protection working, including how teams are staffed and assigned, how protection is set for a given person and situation, what we spend and which vendors we use, what people are trained to do, and how incidents get handled.
This is a player-coach role, and the coaching half does not keep you off the field. You will work advances, travel with the people we protect, and take your turn in the rotation while setting the standard the team works to. Protection here is a service. It works when the people we protect can move through their lives with as little friction as we can manage, and when they trust the team enough to tell us what we need to know.
You own protective operations, training and standards, vendor management, incident response, and converged physical-cyber protection. Protective teams, intelligence, and cybersecurity work on the same problem simultaneously, and detection and intelligence capabilities drive our protective posture.
Success in the first year means a tight operating rhythm, training and qualification standards that hold up against the best protective programs, a team that is current and deployable on short notice, and protective decisions driven by intelligence rather than reaction.
You are excited about this opportunity because you will…
Lead protective operations. Own staffing, assignment, protective decisions, resourcing, and response across the full scope of the program. Lead from within the work rather than from above it, and be accountable for how it performs.
Own training and standards. Set what people are trained on, qualified in, and expected to keep current, then verify it is happening and hold the records that prove it. Build a team that deploys on short notice and stays that way.
Own vendor and supplier management. Decide what we need and from whom, run competitive procurement, and set approval thresholds. Where a supplier is part of how we protect someone, they meet our standard.
Own incident response. Be the escalation point for protective events within your authority and make real-time calls on protection and resourcing. Escalate immediately on legal exposure, law enforcement involvement, or risk that reaches other teams, and write down what was decided and why.
Lead converged physical-cyber protection. Work with Protective Intelligence and Cyber Protective Services to read threat indicators and judge what testing and assessment findings actually mean. When a threat starts online, you decide how protection answers it.
Earn trust and keep friction low. Build relationships with the people we protect, their families, and their teams to make protection something they rely on rather than tolerate. Design the friction out, so we ask less of them for the same result.
We are excited about you because you bring…
Leadership and operating experience. Ten or more years in protective, security, or military operations, including five or more years managing people with hands-on responsibility for protective operations. You have held real decision authority, not advised someone who held it, and you are still close enough to the work to run it yourself.
Judgment under pressure. You make sound calls with incomplete information in fast-moving, high-consequence situations, and the record of those decisions holds up under later review.
Building, not inheriting. A track record of building or scaling protective capability and setting the standards, qualifications, and procedures other leads work to.
Breadth of scope. Experience running more than one protective discipline or program at the same time, including through other leads, accountable for cost, method, and staffing across all of it.
Technical fluency across physical and cyber security. You do not need to be a security engineer, but you need to think like one. You understand how networked systems are put together and how someone would go about taking them apart, you are comfortable with network security concepts, access control, surveillance, and residential security technology at the operational level, and you can tell whether a proposed fix actually closes the gap it claims to.
Service orientation and discretion. You have earned the confidence of the people you protect and the people close to them, and you have kept it. You handle sensitive information about who is protected, how, and where without exception.
Working well across teams. A record of partnering with intelligence, cybersecurity, legal, and business teams on matters that go beyond your authority.
Availability. Willingness to travel around 35 percent, with peaks near 50 percent, often on short notice, and to pick up the phone on protective events and serious escalations outside working hours.
Physical readiness for the work. The ability to stay on your feet and moving for long stretches across offices, residences, venues, and transit, to lift and carry equipment up to 50 pounds, to assist or move a person to safety, to work in tight spaces and sit in vehicles and aircraft for extended periods, to see and assess people, vehicles, and conditions at distance and in poor light, to communicate clearly in loud environments, and to drive in heavy traffic and bad conditions.
Endurance for the conditions. The ability to work outdoors and in transit in extreme heat, extreme cold, inclement weather, and crowds for as long as the work takes, to work irregular and long hours including nights, weekends, and holidays on short or broken sleep and across time zones, and to keep making good decisions while doing it.
Education. Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
Senior Data Engineer - Schaumburg
MISUMI | Data Platform
Own the data platform that MISUMI runs on
MISUMI is looking for a Senior Data Engineer to be the go-to owner of our Snowflake warehouse, dbt project, and data pipelines. You will be the primary data engineer, with real ownership and real influence: the models you build and the pipelines you run are what Operations, Finance, Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Product, and Customer Support rely on to make decisions every day.
You will work hands-on with a modern stack (Snowflake, dbt, Fivetran, Git/GitHub) and with AI coding agents in your daily engineering work. You will also have the autonomy to take requests from intake to production, propose what we should build next, and shape safe team practices for agentic development. If you want a role where your judgment directly determines whether the business can trust its data, this is it.
Impact in this Role
The Senior Data Engineer is the go-to owner of MISUMI’s Snowflake warehouse, dbt project, and data pipelines. This person turns data from business and production systems into trusted, analytics-ready models that Operations, Finance, Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Product, and Customer Support use to make decisions. Because this is the primary data engineering role, the accuracy, security, and reliability of the data platform, including regulated data such as CUI, depend on this person’s judgment and execution.
Essential Functions
Administer Snowflake: manage users, roles, grants, warehouses, resource monitors and security policies, and keep the environment secure, fast and cost-efficient.
Design, build, and own dbt models (staging, intermediate, marts, and the semantic layer) that turn replicated source data into trusted, analytics-ready tables with tests and documentation.
Build, operate, and monitor ELT pipelines from production and business systems into Snowflake, using Fivetran and related tools. Resolve connector failures, schema changes, backfills, and data-quality issues.
Act as the team’s primary technical resource for modeling and pipeline work. Take requests from intake to production independently, including scoping, estimating, and reporting status.
Translate business requirements into technical requirements and data models, and bridge the gap between business teams and technology. Ask clarifying questions, agree on metric definitions and acceptance criteria with stakeholders, and turn them into specifications the team can build and test.
Proactively identify opportunities where data, modeling, or automation can help the business get closer to its goals, and propose and prioritize them with stakeholders instead of waiting for requests.
Run an impact analysis before changing, deprecating, or removing any shared table, model, or connector. Use dbt lineage, Snowflake dependency and access metadata, and stakeholder review, and document a rollback plan.
Own the Git and GitHub workflow for the dbt project: branching standards, pull-request review, automated tests, and deployment.
Use AI assistants and agentic workflows in daily engineering work to speed up SQL and dbt development, testing, documentation, code review, and debugging, and help set safe team practices for using them.
Find the root cause of data-quality, performance, and pipeline problems and fix them at the source.
Tune queries, models, and warehouse usage, and advise engineers and analysts on efficient query patterns and table design.
Maintain data dictionaries, data-flow diagrams, and schema documentation.
Lead data design sessions and technical reviews, and explain design trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Evaluate new Snowflake and dbt features and tools, and recommend improvements to the data platform.
Mentor analysts and engineers on SQL and dbt best practices.
Work with remote, cross-functional teams across time zones.
Maintain and contribute to the Quality Management System (QMS).
Desired Traits
Five core skills. Candidates must show direct, hands-on production experience in each:
Snowflake administration and engineering: access control, warehouse sizing and cost control, query tuning, clustering, security controls, cloning, time travel, and data sharing.
dbt expert modeling: layered models, dimensional modeling, incremental models, snapshots, macros, tests, documentation, and CI/CD through Git.
Advanced SQL: CTEs, window functions, recursive queries, semi-structured data, and query tuning.
ETL/ELT tooling: Fivetran (our tool) or similar, including connector setup, schema drift, deleted records, backfills, and cost.
Agentic coding and development: daily use of AI coding agents that work in the repository and terminal (not chat-only use), with disciplined verification of everything they produce.
Required
Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
10+ years of experience as a data engineer, designing, building, and operating data pipelines and warehouses.
6+ years of hands-on Snowflake experience in production, including administration: access control, warehouse management, and cost and performance monitoring.
5+ years building and maintaining production dbt projects (dbt Core or dbt Cloud), including testing, documentation, incremental models, macros, and CI/CD.
5+ years working with ETL/ELT tools such as Fivetran, Airbyte, Stitch, Matillion, Informatica, or Talend, plus experience with pipeline orchestration.
Demonstrated, hands-on experience using agentic coding tools that work directly in the codebase (not chat-only AI use) in daily data engineering work. This includes building agentic workflows or tool integrations for data work, such as MCP servers, custom agents, or automated dbt and pipeline checks, with concrete examples of the workflows and results.
Expert SQL, including CTEs, window functions, and performance tuning.
Daily use of Git and GitHub pull-request workflows.
Experience being the primary or sole owner of a data platform, or the technical lead for one.
Experience administering data platforms that hold regulated data (such as CUI under NIST SP 800-171), including access control, audit logging, encryption, and data classification. Must be able to pass a background check and complete required CUI and security training.
Preferred
Direct Fivetran experience, including connector management.
Experience with Sigma Computing, or with Tableau, Looker, or a similar BI tool.
Experience modeling ERP and CRM data, such as NetSuite or Salesforce.
Python for data tooling and automation.
Snowflake SnowPro certification or dbt certification.
Infrastructure-as-code experience for Snowflake, such as Terraform.
Background in manufacturing, supply chain, or marketplace businesses.
Abilities
Write advanced SQL on large, complex datasets, including semi-structured data such as JSON in Snowflake VARIANT columns.
Apply data warehousing and dimensional modeling principles to turn business requirements into well-structured, maintainable models.
Work independently: take an open-ended problem, define the approach, deliver it, and raise risks early instead of stalling.
Use sound production judgment: verify before changing shared systems, plan for failure, and know how to roll back.
Use AI tools with discipline: give clear context and constraints, review and test every AI-generated change, and stay accountable for the result.
Solve hard problems methodically: break an unclear problem into testable hypotheses, gather evidence from logs, lineage, and query history, confirm the cause before changing anything, and verify the fix worked.
Communicate clearly in writing and in person, giving business context to engineers and technical context to non-engineers.
Physical Demands
The employee routinely sits, talks, hears, and uses hands and fingers to operate a keyboard. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Travel
Ability to travel 5% annually in the US for team meetings, offsites, and conferences.
Ready to own the platform?
If you have run production Snowflake, dbt, and ELT at scale, you work daily with agentic coding tools, and you want to be the person the business trusts with its data, we would like to hear from you. Apply today.
Salary range:
$167,000 - $202,300 base salary per year, depending on experience
Benefits include, but are not limited to:
Comprehensive medical and dental coverage
401(k) plan
Generous PTO and leave programs
We’re actively seeking teammates who:
Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.
Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.
Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.
Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins.
Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates
We encourage applications from members of underrepresented groups, including but not limited to women, members of the LGBTQ community, people of color, people with disabilities, and veterans.

title: Electromechanical Technician
description:
Job Description:
SUMMARY
Performs all related duties necessary for maintenance and repair of machinery and equipment used in production plant; for maintenance and repair of the physical structure, electrical, and plumbing systems of the buildings; and, when necessary, performs various construction/remodeling duties to company property as assigned.  Also performs electrical maintenance and repairs of plant production equipment and commercial building.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Follows all company safety rules and policies.
Must be able to maintain 5S program standards including organizing, labeling, cleaning and sustaining of workstations, toolboxes, work areas and parts shelving and cabinets.
Must be able to read, understands and follows schematics, wire and parts diagrams, sketches, operation manuals and manufacturer’s specifications to repair and maintain machinery and mechanical equipment such as, but not limited to, motors, pneumatic, hydraulic, conveyor systems and production machines and equipment using hand tools, power tools and precision measuring and testing instruments.
Observes mechanical devices in operation and listens to their sounds to locate causes of trouble. Root Cause
Dismantles machines or equipment to gain access to and remove defective parts, replaces defective parts and motors, and adjusts feed mechanisms.  Replaces or repairs machine belts.  Performs these duties with the aid of such equipment as hoists, cranes, hand tools and power tools.
Holds scaffolding members in place or tightens bolts to erect working platforms about machines.
Cleans and lubricates machine parts, such as, but not limited to, shafts, pulleys, gears, and bearings, using rags, brushes, grease gun, oil can, and other required tools not specifically listed here.
Removes dust, dirt, grease and waste material from machines.
Painting machines or equipment to prevent corrosion.
May install and repair electrical systems and electrical and electronic components of industrial machinery and equipment, following electrical code, manuals, schematic diagrams, blueprints and other specifications, using hand tools, power tools and electrical and electronic test equipment.
Observes functioning of installed equipment or system to detect hazards and need for adjustments, relocation or replacement.
May diagnose/troubleshoot malfunctioning equipment, such as control circuits, motors and lighting fixtures, HVAC systems, using testing equipment, and make necessary repairs, such as replacing damaged or broken wires and cables. Troubleshoot to component levels
Tests malfunctioning machinery, using test equipment and discusses malfunction with other maintenance employees to diagnose malfunction.  Replaces faulty electrical components of machinery, such as wiring, fuses, relays, switches, electric motor bearings and motors and positions sensing devices.
May diagnose and repair or replace faulty electronic components, such as circuit boards, and mechanical, hydraulic and pneumatic components of machines and equipment.
Maintains tools and equipment and keeps supplies and parts in order.
May repair electronic equipment such as industrial controls, audio systems, transmitters, and servomechanisms, following blueprints and manufacturers’ specifications and using hand tools and test instruments.
Converses with machinery/equipment operators to ascertain problems with machinery/equipment before breakdown and to determine if breakdown is due to human error or mechanical/electrical problems.
Tests faulty machinery/equipment and applies knowledge of functional operation of electronic/electrical systems or units to diagnose cause of malfunction.
Tests electronic components and circuits to locate defects, using oscilloscopes, signal generators, ammeters and voltmeters. Replaces defective components and wiring and adjusts mechanical parts, using hand tools and soldering iron.  Aligns, adjusts and calibrates equipment according to specifications.
Maintains records of repairs, calibrations and tests.
May connect wiring to lighting fixtures and power equipment, using hand tools.  May install control and distribution components such as switches, relays and circuit-breaker panels, fastening in place with screws or bolts, using hand tools and power tools.
May connect power cables to equipment and installs grounding leads.
Tests continuity of circuit to ensure electrical compatibility and safety of components using testing instruments, such as ohmmeter, battery and buzzer and oscilloscope.
May bend and cut conduit and wire, and drill holes in walls, floors and ceilings for electrical connections.
May connect wire to motors, fixtures, and other electrical equipment, replace switches and fuses and splice wire and insulates wire with friction tape.
May bend, cut and thread pipe, cut openings in walls, ceilings and floors for pipes, seal pipe joints with sealing compound.
May cut out and join parts for worktables, benches, shelves and other furnishings, using power tools and hand tools.
May be required to assist with plumbing repair work, building construction/remodeling/repairs, general machinery maintenance or repair duties.
May patch or replace plaster or plaster board and paint walls, ceilings, and trim of building.
May drill and break up concrete.
May mix and pour concrete for foundations.
May weld and fabricate a variety of deigns, including fixtures, carts, tables, and platforms using MIG, TIG and/or stick methods.
Clears clogged drains and replaces plumbing fixtures.
Inspects products and processes while performing job duties to ensure all work done meets or exceeds standards of the company’s quality program.
Works cooperatively and congenially with co-workers to achieve cohesive and productive work processes and work environment.
May provide ground watch for other maintenance employees using aerial equipment
May be required to assist with spill response clean-up
May be required to train other maintenance employees
Performs additional tasks as assigned by management or as the situation requires.
QUALIFICATIONS
Valid Texas Driver’s License required
3 + years’ experience in general mechanical maintenance of production machinery to include reading blueprints, wire diagrams, pneumatics, hydraulics, welding, root cause analysis, and requesting machine parts.
Possess minimum knowledge of electrical wiring repairs and installation, AC/DC controls, blueprints, schematic diagrams, pneumatics, and hydraulics.
Technical degree and/or license relating to electrical, mechanical or HVAC/Refrigeration - minimum of one preferred OR 40 hours of documented electrical training. License number and/or documentation must be provided before hire date.
Must be able to meet all minimum training requirements within first 6-12 months of hire date.
Obtain and Maintain Traulsen/OSHA certifications for powered equipment, including but not limited to, forklifts, scissor lifts, aerial booms, stock chasers, and floor scrubbers within first 90 days of hire date.
Capable of operating aerial lift equipment
Obtain and maintain Traulsen/OSHA certifications for power equipment.
Ability to follow verbal and written instructions regarding procedures required for various machine repair.
Ability to read and follow repair or installation instructions
Ability to use a variety of small hand tools, power tools, scissors lifts, and material handling equipment.
Possess basic mechanical aptitude and ability.
Ability to communicate clearly with co-workers (bi-lingual English-Spanish a plus)
Ability to read and follow written English instructions and complete PMs and work orders within Maintenance CMMS software. Some ability to write English responses.
Ability to understand basic online safety and cyber security courses presented in English and demonstrate understanding through multiple choice exam score
Ability to communicate through email
PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT
Attend work regularly and report promptly for duty on the days and at the times scheduled by the supervisor.
Schedule changes occur and should be handled in a productive manner
Working temperatures vary with seasonal changes where climate control is limited.  The environment is one in which noise exists.
Work occasionally outdoors in temperatures ranging from hot to cold and exposed to rain and wind
Sit on a forklift, stand, walk, squat, climb, or crawl for a combined minimum of eight (8) to ten (10) hours per day on a concrete surface.
Lift and carry components, tools, or other items weighing more than 35 pounds.  Any item over 35 pounds, is to be done with assistance
Pull and push up to 100 pounds.
Ability to work around hazardous chemicals.
Carries tools and equipment to and from storage and work areas.
May perform combination of physical movements to reach areas difficult to access including bending, stooping, squatting, reaching, twisting and rotation motions using head/neck, arms, wrists, waist, knees and arms while performing duties.
Handle small hand tools and power tools.  Handling may be done unilaterally (one-handed) or bilaterally (two-handed) depending on size and shape of object and task being performed.
Need corrected vision to be aware of surroundings and location of items needed and perform various other job duties.
Need corrected hearing to identify conditions in the environment (i.e. forklift horns, fire alarms).
Need mental alertness to identify, avoid, or resolve safety hazards.
Ability to work at elevated heights.
Ability to communicate with supervisors and co-workers.
Ability to wear designated personal protective equipment for the work assignment (i.e. safety glasses, cut-resistant gloves, hearing protection, harnesses, hard hats, safety shoes)
Hours of Work
Monday – Friday, 6:00am – 2:30pm and OT when required including, but not limited to, frequent Saturdays with a schedule of 5:00am – 1:30pm

description:

Smart People. Smart Ideas. Smart Choice.
Hands-On Field Service Role
MTS is a leading global supplier of test and simulation systems. Formula 1 teams, leading automotive and aerospace companies, and the world's top researchers in materials and seismic engineering all rely on our systems to determine product reliability and ensure compliance with quality standards. Check out some of our amazing technology here: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vXOsvWpTHH4
What This Role Looks Like
This is a unique, HQ-based Field Service Engineer role for someone who thrives on variety over a fixed territory. As our floater FSE based in Eden Prairie, MN, you'll step into a trainer's or mentor's territory anywhere in North America for the full duration of each training or mentoring event, keeping coverage seamless while they're out. When no event is active, you'll cover PTO, illness, and peak overflow. Being based at MTS headquarters means faster ramp-up, direct access to SMEs and training resources, and central dispatch to wherever coverage is needed next.
Day to day, the work is hands-on: installing, maintaining, calibrating, and troubleshooting complex servo-hydraulic and electro-mechanical test systems at customer sites. Training on MTS-specific technology is provided, and strong hands-on technical aptitude is essential.
Travel: This role involves frequent travel from home base in Eden Prairie, MN to customer sites across North America, since coverage assignments follow wherever a training or mentoring event or overflow need arises. Travel will vary week to week rather than following a fixed regional pattern, and candidates should be genuinely comfortable with, and energized by, a highly travel-oriented role.
Key Responsibilities
Install, maintain, calibrate, and repair computer-controlled servo-hydraulic and electro-mechanical test systems
Diagnosing issues across controllers, hydraulics, data acquisition systems, sensors, transducers, fixtures, and grips
Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, and control-system issues using hands-on diagnostic methods
Perform calibrations independently for assigned customer systems
Manage service documentation, assigned assets, and customer communication professionally
Work directly with customer engineering and lab teams in a service-oriented environment
Maintain technical training and compliance with MTS quality and safety standards
Who This Role Is a Good Fit For
We are open to candidates at different stages of their careers. The common thread is hands-on technical aptitude, willingness to travel, and interest in growing into an independent field service role. Training and mentorship are provided.
Pathway A: Early-Career Technical Professionals
You may be a good fit if you have:
Hands-on technical experience gained through internships, co-ops, labs, maintenance roles, automation, robotics, manufacturing, or military service (typically 2–4 years combined)
An associate degree in Mechatronics, Mechanical/Electrical Engineering Technology, or similar, or a 4-year Engineering Technology degree
Comfort working with tools, wiring, mechanical assemblies, and technical systems, with interest in growing into an independent field service role
Field service experience is not required for early-career candidates. Structured onboarding, shadowing, and technical training are provided.
Pathway B: Experienced Technicians / Field Service Professionals
You may be a good fit if you bring:
5–10+ years supporting electro-mechanical, hydraulic, or industrial equipment
Experience in field service, installation, system startup, or maintenance
Comfort owning customer relationships and troubleshooting complex systems with minimal supervision
Core Expectations for All Candidates
Comfort with a field-based role involving regular travel, especially during the first year, with increasing flexibility as independence grows
Willingness to learn and follow structured training and mentorship during onboarding
Strong communication skills and professional interaction with customers
Valid driver’s license and ability to meet company vehicle requirements
Experience That Is Helpful (Not Required on Day One)

Calibration, diagnostics, or test-equipment experience
Hands-on mechanical and/or electrical troubleshooting
Familiarity with common electrical and mechanical diagnostic tools and test equipment

HSA/FSA with a company match

Industry leading 401(k) plan
Paid time off
Parental leave

Brooks Instrument ( www.brooksinstrument.com ), an industry leader in flow and pressure instrumentation for critical applications, is seeking candidates for a Production Supervisor (Industrial Products) that will be based at the company headquarters in Hatfield, Pennsylvania (suburban Philadelphia). The company has manufacturing locations in Pennsylvania, California, Hungary, Malaysia and Korea, and also maintains sales and service offices throughout the world. Our high-tech products are used in laboratory and process applications in end markets such as: oil & gas, petrochemical, medical devices, waste water, life sciences, and analytical instruments.
Brooks is a division of ITW (Illinois Tool Works), a fortune 200 company. ITW is one of the world’s leading diversified manufacturers of specialized industrial equipment, consumables, and related service businesses. The company has operations in 56 countries and employs over 50,000 employees. These talented employees, many of whom have specialized engineering or scientific expertise, contribute to ITW’s global leadership in innovation. The company is proud of its broad portfolio of nearly 10,000 active patents, and is focused on fully leveraging its highly differentiated business model to deliver solid growth with consistent best-in-class margins and return on capital.
Basic Function
The 1st shift Production Supervisor provides direct leadership and operational oversight for first- and second-shift employees manufacturing Industrial products at the Brooks Instrument facility in Hatfield, Pennsylvania. Working a schedule designed to provide meaningful coverage and visibility across both shifts, the supervisor ensures consistent execution of safety, quality, delivery, productivity, inventory, cost, housekeeping, and employee-performance expectations.
The supervisor serves as the primary connection between the two shifts, maintaining clear priorities, effective handoffs, and consistent application of policies and operating practices. This role works closely with the Production Operations Manager, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Materials, Supply Chain, Human Resources, and other partners to resolve issues, develop employees, meet customer requirements, and drive continuous improvement through the ITW Toolbox and Lean Manufacturing methods.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
•       Provide direct supervision, daily direction, coaching, and performance management for assigned first- and second-shift employees supporting Industrial production.
•       Maintain a regular work schedule that overlaps first and second shifts sufficiently to provide leadership visibility, employee access, direct observation, communication, and accountability across both shifts.
•       Establish and communicate daily production priorities, staffing assignments, schedules, output requirements, and operational expectations based on customer demand and business needs.

title: Strategic Sourcing Intern - Summer 2027
description:
Job Description:
Since its founding more than 100 years ago, ITW has become one of the world’s leading diversified manufacturers of specialized industrial equipment, consumables, and related service businesses. We place a high premium on the development of innovative solutions–most of which are developed in tandem with our customers. And we continue to ensure that our customers receive timely, cost-effective service for the innovative products we provide.
ITW’s differentiated business model is composed of a set of unique core capabilities: our proprietary 80/20 business process, customer-back innovation, and our well-known decentralized entrepreneurial culture. These capabilities are unmistakably ITW—and key to our longevity and strong performance.
ITW’s products and solutions are at work all over the world, in deep-sea oil rigs, aerospace technology, bridges and wind turbines, healthcare, the spaces in which we live and work, the cars we drive, and the mobile devices we rely on. We are never, whether we know it or not, more than a few steps from an innovative ITW solution.
Today, ITW (NYSE: ITW) is a Fortune 300 global multi-industry manufacturing leader with revenue of $16.0 billion in 2025 and employs ~43,000 people operating in 49 countries . Our headquarters located in Glenview, IL. includes a fitness center at no cost to the employees, a cafe, outdoor volleyball courts, walking trails around the facility, employee resource groups, corporate discounts, dry cleaning services, covered/outdoor parking, and much more. We are just a block away from the nearest Metra station, allowing for an accessible commute to downtown Chicago.
More details on our benefits can be found on our website at https://www.itw.com/careers/benefits-compensation/ .
Internship Program Overview
ITW’s internship program provides unparalleled access to challenging opportunities in high-growth, dynamic industries. Interns are encouraged to think and act like entrepreneurs and are provided with significant responsibility to get things done. As an intern, you will gain substantial personal learning and career development opportunities through ownership of real-world job assignments, strong coaching and support with senior leaders across the Enterprise.
ITW’s “80/20” front-to-back business model along with our entrepreneurial culture will provide you with the opportunity to work in an organization that is committed to innovation and creativity. Our program gives interns the chance to collaborate with their teams and participate in exciting, enterprise-wide projects. Some of our intern engagement highlights include intern kickoff events, professional workshops, lunch & learns, volunteering during ITW’s Day of Action, networking, and more.
Position Summary
ITW’s Internship Program is aimed at providing meaningful and fulfilling work experience under the mentorship of skilled professionals. This summer internship program will provide you with marketable experiences and skills, as well as introduce you to ITW’s unique way of doing business. Excellent performance can result in a full-time employment offer.
Responsibilities
Develop basic understanding of assigned commodities: current market conditions, key cost drivers, global supply base, and industry terminology, as it relates to creating purchasing programs for ITW companies.
Conduct broad market research to identify world-class suppliers for the different commodities to be sourced.
Identify sourcing opportunities to drive savings and cost avoidance via spend analysis, stakeholder interviews, and market trends.
Quantify the benefits of sourcing initiatives including the expected savings and baseline spend.
Influencing key stakeholders on strategy initiatives.
Partner across the organization to improve financial results related to sourcing activities.
Utilize project management skills to create a timeline, set milestones, measure progress, and report findings to team.
Collaborate as part of a cross-functional team that includes members from other Corporate ITW teams such as Spend Management and Trade Compliance.
Qualifications
Rising Junior or Senior students pursuing degree in Business, Supply Chain, or Engineering.
Minimum GPA 3.0.
Strong MS Excel skills, including V-lookup, H-lookup and indexing functions, pivot tables and graphs. Proficient in Microsoft Word and PowerPoint.
Strong communication skills and ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional team.
Resourceful and able to work independently.
Must be detail-oriented and able to cleanse large sets of data (identifying mistakes in address field assignments, etc.).
Present your accomplishments, lessons learned, and insights in briefings to Strategic Sourcing leadership.
This internship is approximately 40 hours per week for 12 weeks, with flexible start and end dates within the range of May-September
Familiarity with artificial intelligence (AI) concepts and tools, with the ability to leverage AI to support research, analysis, problem-solving, and process efficiency.

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
About Intuitive Surgical
Intuitive Surgical is a global leader in minimally invasive care and innovative surgical robotics. We advance the boundaries of medical care by continually fostering an environment rich in discovery, problem-solving, and growth. Our mission is to drive better, safer outcomes for patients, care teams, and hospitals, while cultivating a culture where professionals are empowered and inspired.
Role Summary
We are seeking an exceptional Assistant General Counsel, Intellectual Property, with deep expertise in patent portfolio management, IP-related transactions, and IP counseling.
This role offers the chance to work at the intersection of some of the most exciting technologies in robotics and medtech today: robotic assisted surgery, AI, computer vision, advanced instrumentation, imaging, and digital surgery. As an in-house IP attorney, you would partner directly with world-class engineers, scientists, physicians, and business leaders to help develop IP strategy for technologies that have the potential to improve patient outcomes and transform how surgery is performed around the world.
Intuitive is entering an exciting period of growth as we continue to expand our platforms, integrate AI and digital technologies, and push the boundaries of what is possible in minimally invasive care. If you enjoy working on breakthrough technology, working closely with innovators, and seeing your work directly influence the trajectory of a business and an industry, we invite you to apply to join our dynamic team.
Primary Function of Position
The Assistant General Counsel, IP will lead and manage an active patent portfolio, including management of patent application preparation, patent prosecution, and IP strategic development to identify and protect Intuitive’s valuable innovations.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP will support a wide variety of IP-related transactional matters, including NDAs and other agreements covering collaboration, product development, and suppliers.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP will support strategic deals and investments, such as M&A and licensing, including conducting IP-related due diligence, crafting and negotiating deal agreements, and advising on IP-related deal strategies.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP will provide additional comprehensive IP-related legal support, including: litigation support (as needed), trademark protection, and trade secret protection.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP l will engage directly with engineers, scientists, management, clinical specialists, and executives, to translate technology developments into strong IP protection and support key business objectives.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP should become informed on industry trends and provide advice about industry and regulatory developments as well as development and implementation of operational and risk management processes and procedures.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP will report to the Associate General Counsel, IP Strategy, and must escalate issues, as appropriate, and partner with all legal team members.
The Assistant General Counsel, IP must represent Intuitive Surgical with external parties with professionalism and strategic insight, including customers, regulators, affiliates, and industry trade groups
Job/Skill Requirements
Minimum of 10+ years experience in intellectual property law as a practitioner at a law firm and/or in-house legal department experience, with a substantial focus on patent prosecution.
At least 2+ years of in-house counsel experience strongly preferred, where responsibilities included patent portfolio management as well as IP-related transactions (with support of litigation and due diligence a plus).
Technical degree, professional background, and/or significant experience related to medical devices, robotics, mechanical engineering, or a related field (electrical engineering or other engineering specialties considered).
J.D. degree and membership in good standing with the California bar or eligible for immediate registration as a Registered In House Counsel “RHIC”.
Admitted to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office.
Ability to assess legal and business opportunities and risks related to IP assets in support of M&A, investment opportunities, licensing, and purchasing or selling of patent portfolios.
Exceptional communication and writing skills, able to distill complex technical and legal concepts for varied audiences.
Ability to closely manage outside counsel and control matter costs.
Willingness to travel on occasion as required.
Other Personal Characteristics:
Engaging, courageous, and self-directed, accustomed to managing with a collaborative, fact-based approach.
Collaborative, resourceful and adaptable—able to anticipate needs and navigate a rapidly changing environment.
Intellectually curious and eager to learn new areas of law and technology and apply knowledge effectively.
If you are ready to make an impact at the forefront of surgical technology innovation—and you have the drive to expand your expertise with a world-class team—we encourage you to apply.

 Discover: Engage multidisciplinary customer stakeholders, commercial teams, and cross-
functional partners to understand patient journeys, program needs, and barriers to

 Synthesize: Identify common needs and successful practices from customer and field
insights that can inform initiatives for broader audiences.
 Design: Develop program strategies, curriculum, and learning activities that help
customers and sales teams apply insights and implement best practices.
 Engage/Promote: Develop and execute integrated internal and external communication
and deployment strategies that drive awareness, utilization, and value realization.

supporting substantiation, and manage regulatory, clinical affairs, and legal review and
approval.

initiatives. Coach customer speakers on presentation structure, content, and delivery,
and partner with Field Marketing, Event Management, and Sales to deliver programs,
deploy resources, and support customer follow-through.
 Evaluate: Measure program and resource utilization and impact using qualitative and
quantitative data and customer and field feedback. Manage assigned budgets and
identify opportunities to improve results and resource use.
 Summarize: Deliver clear, compelling presentations to senior and executive Intuitive
leadership and other stakeholders. Report outcomes objectively and translate findings
into actionable recommendations.
- Refine and Scale: Use results and feedback to improve effectiveness, reinforce adoption,
and scale successful approaches. Recommend when to refresh, consolidate, or retire
programs and resources.

Professional Expereince:
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in marketing, sales, sales training, product
management, or hands-on service line development preferred.
- Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business Administration, Life Sciences, or a related field
required; Master’s degree preferred.
- Experience coaching physicians and executives on presentation content, structure, and
delivery.
- Proven track record developing and deploying integrated internal and external
communication plans tailored to stakeholder priorities and needs.
- Experience independently authoring marketing content, developing claims, mapping
supporting substantiation, and managing regulatory, clinical affairs, and legal review.

- Demonstrated ability to define success measures, design surveys, and combine
customer and field insights with utilization, adoption, and performance data to quantify
marketing impact and guide actionable recommendations.
- Hands-on experience planning and delivering in-person and virtual education programs,
including society events, workshops, and webinars.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite required; experience with Adobe Creative Cloud
applications preferred.

- Strong discovery and analytical skills, with a deep understanding of customer journeys and
healthcare decision-making processes.
- Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to make complex
information clear, compelling, and actionable in both in-person and virtual formats.
- Strong project management skills, with the ability to coordinate and execute programs
through influence vs. authority across a matrixed organization.
- Ability to build strong relationships with customers, key opinion leaders, marketing and
sales teams, and cross-functional partners
- Self-directed, with sound judgment and the ability to solve open-ended problems.
- Strong desire to enable others’ success and support sales teams in achieving their goals.
- Strong tactical execution skills with a desire to contribute to strategy.

Some experience in an academic environment conducting literature searches, reviews and appraisal of scientific data.
