In CSS, we are powered by Microsoft’s AI technology to help consumers, businesses, partners, and more, resolve their issues quickly and securely, helping prevent future problems from occurring and achieving more from their Microsoft investment.
In the Customer Service & Support (CSS) organization we are looking for people with a passion for delivering customer success. As a Senior Support Escalation Manager, you will be the primary contact managing escalated customer and partner issues. This opportunity will allow you to accelerate your career growth, hone your problem-solving, collaboration and orchestration skills, and deepen your relationship management expertise.
The Senior Support Escalation Manager (Service Manager) is positioned and aligned with our customers as Chief Operating Officers within the account, strategically placed to ensure that we have the appropriate level of engagement to support and drive the customer’s reactive support landscape and improve operational health. I work with some of the world’s largest companies, public sector depts and not for profit organizations pursuing strategic activities, utilizing Microsoft technologies to modernize their business.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Account Escalation Partner
Owns the reactive support experience for a defined set of strategic or mission critical accounts, often funded directly by the customer. Acts as the primary escalation and crisis contact for those accounts, orchestrating internal and external stakeholders (Customer Success Account Managers [CSAMs], engineering, incident managers, legal/PR, executives) to resolve high impact issues while representing the customer’s business impact. Proactively assesses account risk, maintains and tests incident response plans (e.g., Major Incident Response Plans [MIRPs]), and run drills or “Get to Green” plans to prevent recurrence and improve overall account health. Maintains a deep, ongoing relationship with designated customers’ executive and technical leaders, enabling them to anticipate escalations, influence architecture and operations, and shift conversations from reactive to strategic. Collaboration
Collaborates with engineering teams and/or operations teams to identify the right resource. Acts as a subject matter expert on the written protocol to ensure the right groups are engaged to resolve customer issues. Builds and enhances technical contacts, SME’s and leaders who can assist in identifying proper resources to assist with issues that cross-Strategic Business Unit (SBU) responsibility. Owns escalated issues and manages account-aligned customer incidents to identify and remove barriers. Ensures existing processes are not a blocker to customer issue resolution and acts as a key player during process improvement efforts. Mentors other Support Escalation team members on how to handle moderate to highly complex cases. Leads moderate to highly complex incidents (and customers) with minimal guidance, navigating ambiguity, incomplete information, and high-stress environment (customer, account team, leadership, etc.) Acts as the single point of accountability for complex, high?impact escalations, removing blockers, accelerating decision?making, and ensuring alignment across engineering, support, and leadership teams. Works with partners to ensure operational rhythm during incidents, including checkpoints, ownership, and escalation updates. Mentors others in structured incident leadership, beyond only case handling. Communication
Takes ownership of and nurtures relationships with internal teams and partners and proactively communicates with senior leadership on issues complex in scope and provides solutions to resolve them. Establishes long-term partnerships with other Strategic Business Units (SBU)s, and builds bridges to keep consistent, uniform engagement from account teams to SBU(s). Manages customer and field expectations around issue response and represents the company independently, prioritizing security as a key component of customer satisfaction. Ensures customer and MSFT internal stakeholders stay informed on the response and resolution status of customer issues. Communicates and influences internally to drive faster issue resolution, incorporating effective security practices to mitigate risks. Provides definitive updates to teams involved as required (e.g., account, Customer Success Account Manager [CSAM], Technology Managers, Leadership, and Executive Leadership). Critical Event Response Manager
Manages incidents and escalations as discrete transactions, focusing on rapid stabilization and resolution rather than ongoing account ownership, with engagement spanning varying levels of technical depth. Works directly with the customer or through support teams to ensure customers are informed, expectations are set, and escalation pressure is effectively managed throughout the incident lifecycle. Leads or supports bridge operations and crisis communications for escalated incidents or critical situations, ensuring consistent, accurate, and timely updates across customers, executives, and engineering, while maintaining compliance with legal, privacy, and communications standards. Drives coordination of technical resources, enforces adherence to processes, and de?escalates distressed customers, often operating across queues spanning multiple customers or specific incident types. Owns incident communications, customer, governance, and post?incident insights. Customer Resolution
Identifies trends across internal postmortems and suggests resources to drive opportunities within the team and across stakeholder groups in post-incident review discussions to remediate future issues. Identifies risks surfaced during escalations and ensures they are routed to proper governance channels within or outside of their Strategic Business Unit (SBU). Ensures remediation includes thorough root cause analysis and any corrective follow-ups required. Acts on or plays a key role in strategic projects designed to improve resolution times, customer satisfaction, and support experience. Implements AI tools to monitor, evaluate, and automate routine tasks, proposing enhancements to boost efficiency and satisfaction. Identifies systemic breakdowns across escalation workflows, handoffs, and decision points, and drives cross?team improvements to increase speed, accountability, and consistency. Champions automation and standardization of escalation workflows to improve scale and consistency. Creates home-grown solutions for intake, tracking and reporting for customer businesses. Provides status updates to customers and internal stakeholders through various channels of communication regarding issues, following the documented process. Utilizes AI-driven communication tools streamline interactions with stakeholders. Coordinates and communicates the escalation narrative, ensuring stakeholder alignment and driving Confidence Calls to either retain customers, solidify renewals, or take direct feedback on the product or support. Drives consistent, executive-ready escalation narrative, aligning all stakeholders on problem statement, impact, risks, and next actions. Acts as a primary contact to understand issues and improve the experiences of customers independently. Maintains and develops relationships with various internal and external teams to resolve customer issues. Mentors others on the Support Escalation Management team. Acts as a key member of projects to drive key strategic initiatives. Manages incidents, which are customer-impacting issues that require coordination, communication, and stakeholder/resource management to drive timely resolution. Owns the end-to-end escalation lifecycle, where escalations are incidents that require elevated visibility or intervention that involve direct engagement with customers or senior stakeholders, including intake, triage, prioritization, resolution, and follow-up. Supports the lifecycle of incidents, which is the coordination, communication, and stakeholder/resource management. Represents Microsoft, Leadership or Strategic Business Unit (SBU) Leaders on internal/external calls. Exercises independent judgment to prioritize escalations based on customer impact, business risk, and urgency. Ensures accountability for escalation outcomes. Acts as a key player when supporting initiatives by gathering feedback and identifying resources to improve the customer support experience for a group of customers or a specific region/area. Models best practices to support the customer experience, including proactively addressing security needs according to Microsoft’s security standards. Leverage AI-driven sentiment analysis tools to gather real-time feedback, identify common customer pain points, and suggest proactive measures for enhancing customer service. Proactively identifies escalation risk signals by reviewing sentiment analysis results, historical escalation data, and customer feedback. Translates customer feedback, escalation themes, and sentiment data into actionable insights that inform leadership decisions and long?term experience improvements. Process Improvement
Creates an executive summary detailing the customer issue, impact on the business, and status of the resolution. Identifies patterns in customer issues and supports the delivery of strategies to resolve them. Joins and shares best practices to improve delivery and improve team performance. Identifies systematic issues and process breakdown and participates in a project or workgroup to improve systematic issues and internal processes. Actively shares new or potential changes to processes that could impact escalation delivery. Regional or Area Support Leader
Owns critical customer recovery and escalation management efforts across a region, vertical, subsidiary, or segment. Aggregates patterns from escalations, delivery results, and post incident reviews to identify systemic issues, operational health risks, and process breakdowns. Drives regional or vertical Get to Green and improvement plans with Customer Service and Support (CSS), field, and Customer Success Unit (CSU) leadership. Operationalizes Crisis Prevention and Management programs across the field. Owns the development and orchestration of Customer Trust Recovery activities. Acts as the regional “voice of the customer” for reactive support, facilitating forums, managing key stakeholder relationships, and aligning CSS priorities with field and business goals, including revenue, consumption, and renewal outcomes. Leads cross team and cross region initiatives, establishes protocols and networks to accelerate resolution, and fosters sustainable changes in support quality and customer trust at scale Technical Recovery and Stabilization Leader
Leads technical recovery for complex and high-impact customer situations, executing and coordinating “get-to-green” recovery plans across multiple issues and teams. Supports and contributes to the diagnosis of root causes, orchestration of cross-functional technical resources, and restoration of service stability and customer confidence. Focuses primarily on the scope of individual or closely related incidents, contributing to multi-issue recovery scenarios that may span extended timeframes and require sustained technical coordination. Owns time-bound engagements within defined recovery scopes and drives progress toward stability and agreed outcomes. Partners with designated customers’ executive and senior technical leaders to align on recovery approach, anticipate and mitigate future escalations, and inform architecture and operational decisions that improve long-term stability. Utilizes deep technical expertise, structured recovery planning, and the ability to align support, engineering, and account teams around clear actions and priorities, influencing recovery efforts within their area of responsibility and helping shift conversations from reactive issue resolution to more proactive, strategic engagement. Identifies patterns and underlying drivers observed during recovery engagements and shares insights and recommendations with relevant teams to contribute to broader improvement efforts while remaining focused on technical recovery execution. Vendor Relationships
Engages with outsourced Customer Service and Support [CSS] delivery partner specialists as part of standard support incident management and escalation resolution activities, not including the management, supervision, or direction of delivery partner resources beyond activities directly related to incident and escalation management coordination. Focuses partner engagements on coordinating efforts across teams, aligning stakeholders, and driving timely resolution of customer issues through effective collaboration, communication, and escalation management.     Other:
Embody our culture and values
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Master's Degree in technology, business, or related field AND 3+ years technology industry, customer service, or related experience  OR Bachelor's Degree in technology, business, or related field AND 4+ years technology industry, customer service, or related experience
OR 7+ years technology industry, customer service, or related experience years of technology industry, customer service, or related experience
OR equivalent experience

We partner with researchers, data scientists, engineers, and cross-functional teams to understand AI’s effects on people’s lives, including well-being, youth experiences, and social and emotional use.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Applied Scientist to help design, execute, and analyze large-scale longitudinal research on AI use and well-being. You’ll work closely with research leads to translate scientific questions into rigorous studies, combining survey responses with behavioral data to understand how people’s experiences with AI evolve over time.

This is a hands-on role spanning applied analysis, research methods, and study execution. You’ll build reproducible analytical workflows, assess data quality and representativeness, and help establish reliable infrastructure for ongoing panel research. Your work will support research involving teens and adults, including studies of AI companionship, and help turn findings into useful evidence for product, policy, and safety partners.

In this role, you will:

 - Partner with research leads to develop study designs, survey measures, and analysis plans for longitudinal research on AI use and well-being.

 - Conduct statistical analyses of survey and behavioral data, including evaluating selection and response bias, account-linkage patterns, and sample representativeness.

 - Prepare and validate analysis-ready datasets, implement analysis plans, and produce clear summaries and visualizations using reproducible workflows.

 - Develop quality checks across survey programming, fieldwork, data delivery, and repeated study waves to identify inconsistencies and improve research reliability.

 - Own day-to-day study execution, coordinating timelines, vendors, and cross-functional dependencies to deliver high-quality research on schedule.

 - Collaborate with data engineering and privacy partners on responsible account linkage, data flows, logging, and retention.

 - Support human-subjects research review, including Institutional Review Board (IRB) documentation, protocol amendments, and consent and assent processes.

 - Maintain clear documentation of methods, measures, assumptions, and protocol changes, and contribute analysis and methodological materials for research readouts, publications, and peer review.

 - Communicate findings, limitations, and practical recommendations to technical and nontechnical partners, and build reusable tools and processes that improve future studies.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have experience conducting applied quantitative research in social science, behavioral science, human-computer interaction, statistics, or a related field.

 - Bring strong foundations in survey research and statistical analysis, with experience working on panel studies, longitudinal datasets, or human-subjects research.

 - Are comfortable using SQL and Python or R to prepare data, implement analyses, validate results, and create visualizations.

 - Understand how recruitment, missing data, participant attrition, and measurement choices can affect the interpretation and generalizability of findings.

 - Can move between analytical work and practical execution, managing multiple timelines and collaborators while maintaining scientific rigor.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Product & Research Communications team helps people understand our technology, what it makes possible, and how to use it. We bring new products and research to the world and tell stories about the people making these tools their own.

We work closely with our Culture & Community Engagement team to connect our products with people’s interests, ambitions, and everyday lives. Together, we help more people discover what they can create, learn, and do with AI—and bring their experiences back into how we communicate.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Community Communications Lead to bring OpenAI’s products closer to communities and help their stories reach a wider audience. Sitting on the Product & Research Communications team, you’ll work hand in hand with the Culture & Community team to shape narratives, develop earned media opportunities, and amplify community-driven stories across organic communications channels.

You’ll be involved from the beginning of campaigns and community programs, bringing ideas that strengthen the story, cultural relevance, and opportunities for participation. Working closely with Culture & Community Engagement leaders, you’ll contribute communications strategy while respecting their ownership of campaign and creative decisions.

You’ll also connect individual campaigns, partnerships, and community moments into a broader story that develops over time. You’ll have the judgment to know when the work has earned a larger conversation—and the relationships and storytelling skills to make it happen.

We’re looking for someone with cultural curiosity, strong editorial taste, initiative, judgment and an entrepreneurial approach. You understand what makes people care and how community trust is built. You keep our claims grounded, can navigate skepticism about AI and understand how a story can invite people to take part.

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission. The Compute & Infrastructure team shares financial insights and partners with internal and external business stakeholders to manage the accounting and financial reporting for OpenAI’s rapidly evolving infrastructure investments.

The team supports a broad and increasingly complex portfolio of compute and infrastructure arrangements, including cloud computing, data centers, servers, equipment, rack financing, colocation arrangements, and other AI infrastructure deployments. We are responsible for ensuring financial accuracy, operational scalability, and informed decision-making as OpenAI continues to invest in advanced technologies and expand its infrastructure footprint.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced and technically skilled accounting professional to manage the accounting and financial reporting for OpenAI’s compute and infrastructure lease-related activities. In this role, you will own complex lease accounting matters across data centers, servers, equipment, and other infrastructure arrangements, while helping operationalize new programs as the organization continues to scale.

You will evaluate unique and highly structured transactions, assess their accounting implications, and translate technical conclusions into clear recommendations for leadership. You will also work cross-functionally to design the processes, systems, controls, and data solutions required to support accurate and scalable accounting operations.

This role requires a strong command of US GAAP, particularly lease accounting and consolidation, as well as the ability to operate effectively and fluidly in an evolving environment where new infrastructure programs may not yet have established processes or system solutions. Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. We’re looking for an Electrical Engineer to develop the AI inference compute systems that power OpenAI’s humanoid robots. This role combines compute architecture, high-speed digital design, onboard power electronics, and compact HDI PCB development.

We’re looking for a self-driven engineer who takes ownership from concept through deployment. Above all, you should enjoy hands-on engineering: bringing up boards, characterizing interfaces, and tracking challenging failures to their root cause.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own compute hardware architecture and development, from component selection and schematic design through PCB layout, validation, and deployment.

 - Design and integrate high-speed interfaces—including PCIe, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, USB, and DisplayPort—balancing bandwidth, connectivity, power, and signal integrity.

 - Define HDI PCB stackups, dielectric materials, via structures, and routing strategies that balance electrical performance, manufacturability, reliability, and cost.

 - Lead bench bring-up and validation, including test planning, high-speed interface characterization, power measurements, and debugging through verified resolution.

title: Electrical Engineer, PCBA Test Infrastructure, Robotics
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking an Electrical Engineer for a senior individual-contributor role leading printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) test infrastructure for advanced robotic systems. You will independently turn evolving requirements into working test stations, make technical tradeoffs, and own delivery from architecture and circuit design through validation, deployment, and reliable operation.

This role combines development-lab work with deployment at contract manufacturers. You will develop electrical test systems for board bring-up, programming, functional test, and characterization, partnering with mechanical, firmware, software, manufacturing, and reliability teams to carry validated stations from prototypes into repeat builds.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week. Travel to contract-manufacturer sites is part of the role, with timing based on build and deployment needs.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own PCBA test-station architecture, including device-under-test interfaces, programmable power, electronic loads, signal routing, instrumentation, and protection.

 - Translate board requirements and likely failure modes into test coverage, measurement methods, and pass/fail criteria. Partner with board designers on design for test, test-point access, programming interfaces, and diagnostics.

 - Design and bring up fixture interface boards, switching circuits, harnesses, and connectors. Release schematics, PCB layouts, wiring diagrams, bills of materials, and interface definitions.

 - Integrate oscilloscopes, meters, power supplies, loads, and data acquisition hardware; validate calibration, timing, accuracy, and repeatability across stations and board revisions.

 - Develop and debug programming and communications interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, and Ethernet as required by the board. Diagnose power, signal-integrity, grounding, and contact problems.

 - Design and validate current limiting, power sequencing, ESD protection, interlocks, and fault recovery appropriate to the hardware under test.

 - Partner with mechanical engineers on probe access, connector mating, board support, cooling, and serviceability. Work with firmware and software partners to define interfaces and integrate test stations with shared software.

 - Write, debug, and maintain test code for instrument control, board programming, automated sequences, diagnostics, and result logging. Collaborate with software partners on reusable frameworks, code reviews, and reliable releases.

 - Establish station commissioning, calibration, maintenance, and configuration control. Track board identity and revision, firmware version, test limits, and station configuration with each result.

 - Use reference boards, independent measurements, and deliberate fault checks to distinguish board failures from fixture or software errors. Improve test coverage, false-failure rate, cycle time, and station uptime.

 - Own test-station deployment and acceptance at contract manufacturers, including station correlation, build support, operator training, and troubleshooting. Release configurations and documentation that keep lab and factory results consistent.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have strong intuition for analog and digital circuits, power delivery, electronics debugging, and reliable measurement.

 - Move comfortably from architecture and circuit design to soldering, probing, scripting, and troubleshooting in the lab.

 - Care about grounding, shielding, contact quality, calibration, and evidence that a test detects the faults it is intended to find.

 - Take ownership from prototype through reliable daily operation, balancing rapid iteration with clear documentation and maintainable test systems.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Demonstrated ability to independently deliver significant electronics test-system projects from ambiguous requirements through working hardware, validation, and sustained use.

 - Hands-on capability in circuit and fixture-interface design, schematic interpretation, board bring-up, power delivery, signal switching, and instrument integration.

 - Ability to independently debug PCBAs and test hardware using oscilloscopes, meters, logic analyzers, and systematic root-cause investigation.

 - Ability to write, debug, and maintain code that interfaces with real hardware in Python or a comparable language, including instrument control, sequencing, error handling, and structured result logging.

 - Practical understanding of grounding, signal integrity, calibration, measurement uncertainty, ESD controls, power sequencing, and electrical protection.

 - Ability to release clear test and hardware documentation, coordinate across engineering disciplines, and support hands-on deployment and troubleshooting at contract manufacturers.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

About the Team

As AI becomes capable of doing more useful work, the way people access and pay for it needs to evolve. Monetization Platform is a new team within Growth building the systems and experiences that make that possible across the entire suite of OpenAI products. Our mission is to make powerful AI easier to access, its value easier to understand, and new ways of using it easier to bring to market.

We work where product experience, platform architecture, and business strategy meet. A new plan or pricing model can change what customers can accomplish—and requires careful engineering across eligibility, entitlements, usage, and subscriptions. We turn that complexity into capabilities that product teams can build on and experiences that customers can trust.

Working with Product, Design, Finance, Financial Engineering, and Data Science, we’re shaping a platform that can evolve alongside our models and products. This is an opportunity to help define a new team’s technical direction and build systems that expand what OpenAI can offer.

 

About the Role

We’re looking for experienced Staff+ and Senior engineers who combine full-stack product instincts with strong backend and systems depth. You’ll help decide what to build, establish the architecture, and carry ideas through to working products—from a customer’s first interaction with a plan to the services that determine what they can access and use.

The work spans new pricing and packaging capabilities, plan and usage experiences, and the shared UIs and tools that make launches repeatable. You’ll partner closely with Financial Engineering to connect these capabilities to subscription and billing systems, keeping customer access and state consistent as offerings evolve.

You’ll have substantial ownership over technical decisions and delivery in an area where the roadmap is still taking shape. Your impact will show up in the experiences you ship, the engineering work you eliminate from future launches, and the opportunities your systems make possible.

 

In this role, you will:

 - Define and build shared pricing and packaging capabilities, including plan configuration, eligibility, entitlement integrations, and usage allowances.

 - Create intuitive plan and usage experiences across the stack, connecting polished interfaces to product APIs and backend services.

 - Turn new commercial ideas into working prototypes and experiments with Product, Finance, and Data Science, then use what you learn to guide the next iteration.

 - Design integrations with Financial Engineering that preserve correct access and subscription state through plan changes, migrations, asynchronous updates, and partial failures.

 - Build reusable components and configuration tools that let teams launch offerings with less custom engineering and fewer dependencies.

 - Take responsibility for production quality through migration planning, staged rollouts, testing, monitoring, and recovery paths.

 - Shape the technical roadmap, make clear tradeoffs between immediate launches and shared foundations, and develop other engineers through code and design reviews.

 - Have set architectural direction and delivered significant projects involving multiple teams, while remaining an active contributor to the code.

 - Bring depth in backend or distributed systems and can work across the APIs and interfaces that turn those systems into useful products.

 - Reason rigorously about data models, lifecycle transitions, consistency, concurrency, and what happens when an operation fails or runs twice.

 - Combine product intuition with experimentation and analysis, and care about whether customers understand and benefit from what you build.

OpenAI’s Benefits team helps attract, support, and retain the people advancing our mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Leaves & Accommodations Analyst to support the day-to-day administration of OpenAI’s leave of absence and workplace accommodations programs. You will coordinate assigned cases from intake through closure, keep records and documentation organized, and support accurate, timely handoffs across the teams involved.

This is a hands-on, employee-facing role for someone who enjoys careful execution and helping people understand what comes next. You’ll follow established policies and workflows, take responsibility for routine case tasks, and recognize when a complex, sensitive, or unclear request needs guidance from the appropriate case owner.

You will partner closely with HR Business Partners, Payroll, HR Systems, third-party administrators, and other members of the Benefits team. This role reports to the Senior Manager, Global Leave & Accommodation.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Coordinate assigned leave cases. Support intake, documentation follow-up, case tracking, return-to-work coordination, and closure for U.S. and international requests, including medical, parental, and statutory leaves. Use established workflows and seek guidance when requirements are unclear.

 - Help employees navigate the process. Provide clear, empathetic updates about required information, timelines, and next steps. Respond to routine employee and manager questions using approved guidance, and route questions outside your scope to the right partner.

 - Support the accommodations process. Organize required information, coordinate follow-ups, and document approved next steps for ergonomic, disability-related, and religious accommodations. Handle medical documentation only through approved confidential channels. Escalate eligibility questions, policy exceptions, legal requirements, and accommodation determinations to the appropriate case owner.

 - Coordinate work across partners. Track outstanding actions with third-party administrators, vendors, HR Business Partners, Payroll, and HR Systems. Make next steps and handoffs clear, follow up on open items, and keep the case owner informed of blockers.

 - Stay on top of deadlines and requests. Keep case trackers current, prioritize routine work against established deadlines, and raise competing priorities or urgent employee needs to your manager early.

 - Improve day-to-day execution. Identify recurring issues and suggest practical changes to checklists, templates, and documentation. Help implement approved improvements that reduce errors and make the process easier for employees and partners.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have hands-on experience supporting leave of absence, workplace accommodations, or related HR operations, including case administration, employee inquiries, or confidential records.

 - Bring working familiarity with U.S. leave and accommodations concepts, such as FMLA, ADA, and applicable state or local requirements, and know when to consult approved guidance or ask for help.

 - Are drawn to detail-oriented, employee-facing work. You enjoy keeping cases organized, following through on commitments, and helping people understand their next steps.

 - Can manage multiple cases, dates, documents, and follow-ups while maintaining accurate records and raising deadline risks early.

 - Have practical experience with an HRIS or case-management system and use spreadsheets to check data. Workday experience is helpful.

 - Communicate clearly and empathetically with employees, managers, and cross-functional partners, making responsibilities and next steps explicit.

The Enterprise Platforms pod runs the SaaS applications employees rely on to communicate, collaborate, and manage work. The pod owns application administration, configuration, integrations, operational controls, and complex escalations. We work across Google Workspace, GCP, Slack, Atlassian and service-management tools, ChatGPT Enterprise, and other enterprise applications, partnering with IT Support, Systems Engineering, Identity & Access Foundations, Security, and business teams.

We’re looking for an IT Systems Engineer to join our Enterprise Platforms pod, with deep experience in platforms such as Google Workspace, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Slack, and a focus on application integration, automation, and internal tools. You’ll connect services across the application portfolio, build tools that simplify work for employees and IT, and own improvements from discovery and design through implementation, rollout, and ongoing operation. Build reusable modules, bring existing resources under management, and detect and reconcile configuration drift. Use APIs and automation for capabilities outside provider coverage.

 - Design, build, and maintain integrations across enterprise applications and cloud services. Own data flows, API access, OAuth clients, service accounts, error handling, and operational monitoring. Partner with cloud and security owners on project setup, permissions, credential handling, and technical handoffs.

 - Build and improve enterprise application integrations and Jira/service-management workflows for IT, Security, and business teams. Translate operational needs into maintainable configurations, routing, approvals, and automation.

 - Validate changes through complete employee workflows. Plan rollouts with monitoring and rollback, establish support ownership, and measure reliability, reduced manual effort, and fewer repeat escalations.

 - Have engineered enterprise platforms at scale, combining hands-on configuration, permissions, and troubleshooting with application integrations, API-based automation, and tools used by employees or IT teams.

title: Research Scientist / Research Engineer, Search - Knowledge Graphs
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models. We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.

The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack: serving, indexing, and retrieval. We research and develop large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to most effectively find and reason over information.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Researcher to work on semi-structured knowledge graphs within Search. You’ll research and develop methods for mining structured information from heterogeneous, unstructured and semi-structured web content, making that information more accessible and useful to AI models.

The core questions are: What structure helps models find and use information? How can we extract it reliably at web scale? And how do we measure whether it improves the model’s ability to reason and answer questions? How do we design the system to be optimizable end-to-end?

You’ll work across research, data, and systems, exploring how advances in AI and compute can improve the way knowledge is extracted, organized, and retrieved. This work will support retrieval across OpenAI products and internal research efforts, with opportunities for scientific publication.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Develop methods to extract and connect structured information across diverse web sources, including entities, attributes, and relationships.

 - Build scalable approaches for transforming noisy, inconsistent content into useful knowledge representations.

 - Explore how models and compute can improve extraction quality and reduce the manual work involved in building knowledge systems.

 - Design evaluations that measure both the quality of extracted knowledge and its usefulness for retrieval and model reasoning.

 - Partner with researchers and engineers to integrate structured knowledge into Search and use model performance to guide improvements.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE

 - Deep experience in knowledge extraction, knowledge graphs, entity resolution, or related work that derives structure from large, heterogeneous datasets.

 - Strong machine learning and research skills, with experience developing and evaluating methods for real-world data.

 - A track record of building or scaling data and ML systems, particularly for web-scale extraction, indexing, or retrieval.

As AI makes convincing content easier to produce at scale, detection systems must adapt to increasingly sophisticated adversaries.

You’ll define the technical approach, build classifiers and evaluations, and shape how integrity signals influence what Search indexes and retrieves. Working closely with Search and broader Safety and Integrity teams, you’ll use frontier models to advance detection methods and bring them into production.

 - Develop AI and ML systems to detect spam, scams, phishing, malicious domains, prompt injections, and other adversarial or low-quality web content.

 - Discover useful signals across page content, links, domains, metadata, and relationships between websites, including patterns that reveal coordinated manipulation.

 - Build evaluations that measure detection quality and how integrity interventions affect the information Search surfaces.

 - Translate detection signals into indexing, ranking, and filtering decisions, improving what models can retrieve and rely on.

 - Serve as the technical owner for integrity within Search, partnering with researchers, engineers, and broader Safety and Integrity teams to build and deploy these systems.

 - Deep experience in web spam, search quality, adversarial content detection, or related integrity problems at scale.

 - Strong applied ML and research skills, with experience developing classifiers, detection methods, and evaluations for real-world systems.

 - An understanding of how adversaries manipulate content and links, coordinate across sites, and adapt to detection systems.

 - A track record of independently defining ambiguous technical problems and driving solutions from experimentation through production.

OpenAI's Safety Research organization works to ensure that our most capable AI models can be deployed safely and responsibly. As frontier models become increasingly capable and autonomous, developing reliable ways to monitor their behavior, identify emerging risks, and evaluate the effectiveness of safety systems becomes increasingly important.

Our work focuses on advancing the research and evaluation methods needed to understand model behavior and ensure that monitoring systems remain effective as model capabilities evolve. We combine rigorous empirical research with practical safety interventions, working closely with research, engineering, and deployment teams to translate findings into improvements across OpenAI's models and products.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a senior researcher to lead technical work on misalignment monitoring for frontier AI systems. You will develop methods to evaluate the effectiveness of AI monitors, understand their limitations, and improve our ability to detect and stop concerning model behavior reliably.

This role combines research leadership with hands-on technical execution. You will set research priorities, design rigorous evaluations, investigate monitoring failures, and develop approaches for stress-testing and improving monitoring systems. A key focus will be understanding where monitors produce false positives, miss important behaviors, or become less effective as models grow more capable.

You will work closely with researchers and engineers across OpenAI to turn monitoring research into practical improvements to our safety systems. We are looking for someone with strong research judgment, technical depth, and the ability to independently drive ambiguous problems from initial investigation through measurable results.

 - Lead the research and technical direction for evaluating and improving the misalignment monitoring of frontier AI systems.

description:
About the Team

The Identity Infrastructure Engineering team builds the identity and access systems that OpenAI’s researchers, engineers, and internal teams rely on to protect critical systems and data.

We partner with Research, Applied Engineering, Infrastructure, IT, and Security to make secure access practical across cloud and internal environments.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands-on software engineer to design and build high-scale, high-throughput secure access proxies and the distributed systems behind them. These are tier-zero services: researchers, engineers, and agents depend on them to reach critical infrastructure safely and reliably.

You’ll work at the intersection of networking, distributed systems, and infrastructure security, building the serving paths and control-plane integrations that connect identities to resources. Teleport is a core part of the current platform; the role also includes credential brokers, policy enforcement, and developer-facing integrations.

You’ll own the services you build from design and implementation through production. That means understanding human, agent, and workload traffic, improving throughput and tail latency, making authorization decisions auditable, and designing for safe multi-region rollout and recovery. We’re looking for someone who can turn a demanding security requirement into software that works well at scale and is straightforward for other engineers to use.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and implement secure access proxies, gateways, and credential brokers that provide narrowly scoped, auditable access to infrastructure and internal services while reducing standing privileges..

 - Integrate identity and access policy across clients, proxies, and target systems so approved permissions take effect promptly and access expires or is revoked when required. Ensure correct behavior when policy is stale or sessions remain active.

 - Build observability that explains the end-to-end access path: latency, errors, saturation, authorization decisions, and identity attribution, without leaking credentials.

 - Engineer safe multi-region rollouts, canaries, rollback, failover, and recovery. Validate changes with realistic test environments, load tests, and failure testing.

 - Keep core access services reliable, performant, and maintainable. Own production support, maintenance, upgrades, and incident recovery; ship durable fixes that reduce recurring failures, alert noise, and manual work.

 - Make secure access easy to adopt through reusable APIs, client tooling, diagnostics, and self-service workflows. Lead migrations that preserve critical workflows, with tested rollback and recovery paths and clear ownership across Infrastructure, Security, and SRE.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

 - Have built and operated production backend, proxy, networking, or infrastructure services with demanding scale or availability requirements.

 - Have practical networking depth and can reason about HTTP, TCP, TLS, DNS, routing, and load balancing across real request paths.

 - Can explain how you handled performance bottlenecks, partial failures, multi-region deployment, or a difficult production change in a system you personally built.

 - Understand authentication, authorization, least privilege, trust boundaries, credential handling, and the consequences of an access-control failure.

 - Have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience with Go, Rust, Python, or similar languages.

 - Use tests, profiling, telemetry, and reproducible experiments to debug across system boundaries and verify correctness, performance, and recovery.

 - Make practical scope decisions, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and follow through from code to production. Teleport or comparable access-platform experience is helpful; strong engineering and production ownership matter more than knowing every tool.

description:

Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.
Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.
About the role
Oura is rebuilding how it builds software. Every engineer has agentic tooling, and our own pipeline already takes a well-formed ticket to a reviewed, tested commit stack. It runs interactively, headless, and on a cloud sandbox fleet, with its own evals and tracing. We are looking for engineers who use AI as a fundamental building block of both the products we ship and the way we build them.
That is a strong start on one stage of the lifecycle. The next step is the whole loop. As a Staff Engineer on the AI Transformation team, you will architect and own the system that turns agentic development from something power users do into the way hundreds of engineers across iOS, Android, backend and AI services ship every day. That means spec and intake, planning, implementation, review, testing, CI/CD, release, observability and incident follow-up, each with agents doing real work and humans keeping judgment where it matters.
This is a fast-moving, LLM-forward team. We prioritize rapid prototyping, iterative loops and AI-native development, with the speed of a startup and the reach of a product used by millions of members. You can work remotely from anywhere in Europe, or hybrid from our offices in Helsinki, Oulu or Tampere.
You will build the pipeline, measure it, and make it trustworthy enough that teams choose it. Success is measured in validated changes reaching members faster and safer: time to a trustworthy signal, escaped defects, cost per merged change, and how many squads run on the paved path because it is better, not because they were told to.
What you will do
You don't need to do all of these on day one, but these are the kinds of problems you'll own:
Set the technical direction for the agentic pipeline: Make our existing ticket-to-PR pipeline dependable infrastructure. Own its architecture, including agent orchestration, context management and tool calling, and improve its reliability, throughput, cost and developer experience across mobile, backend and web repositories. Run it unattended where the risk allows.
Close the loop across the SDLC: Extend agentic workflows beyond code generation into spec quality checks, test generation, automated review, CI failure triage and repair, release verification, and post-deploy signals, so the system improves from what happens after merge.
Prototype fast, then harden: Get a new workflow running in days, prove it on real tickets with real squads, and turn what holds up into production infrastructure.
Run AI in production properly: Agents in production take more than an API call. Own the eval sets, LLM-as-a-judge grading, versioning, tracing and dashboards that tell us whether a workflow change made things better, including the hardest case: a change that passes CI and is still wrong. Track the numbers that matter (merge rate, rework, time-to-signal, cost per change, escaped defects) and make them visible to engineers and leadership.
Make autonomy safe: Design sandboxing, permissions, human checkpoints and guardrails proportional to risk, with privacy by design as the default. Health data, security and infrastructure changes get stronger controls; low-risk, easily verified work runs hands-off.
Lead AI-native engineering by example: Set the bar for AI-augmented engineering across the organization. Show in your own work what a pipeline-first engineer ships, and raise the craft of the engineers around you.
Drive adoption with the teams: Embed with squads and their AI DRIs, find where the pipeline breaks on real work, fix the system rather than the single output, and turn what works into paved paths, skills, templates and docs other engineers can extend.
Partner cross-functionally: Work with platform, developer productivity, security and privacy, AI infrastructure, mobile and backend squads, product and design, and engineering leadership to make trade-offs explicit and keep everyone moving on one system instead of five parallel ones.
Requirements
We'd love to hear from you if you are:
An experienced builder: 6+ years building and operating production systems that other engineers depend on, including developer tooling, internal platforms, or AI infrastructure at scale. We weigh demonstrated outcomes over years.
Proven with agentic loops in production: You have built and operated agentic coding workflows or autonomous loops in a real engineering organization, beyond demos: background agents producing PRs, automated review, CI repair, test generation, or similar, with adoption and measured results.
A whole-lifecycle thinker: You reason about specification, review, testing, CI/CD, release and operations as one system, and you know where the bottleneck moves when code generation gets cheap.
A technical leader: You set direction across teams you don't manage, write the designs others build on, and are trusted with the hard calls on architecture and risk.
Strong on fundamentals: mobile domain or backend APIs, concurrency, distributed systems, testing, debugging and reliability. You treat AI output as a draft and can show how you verify it.
Technically versatile: Fluency in one domain of backend, iOS, or Android, with a stretch into others. You use the tools available to work across platforms and pick up new stacks quickly.
Security and privacy conscious: You understand the responsibility of handling sensitive personal data and of giving agents access to real systems, and you design for both from the start.
High agency: You thrive in ambiguity and shape the requirements yourself through experimentation.
Collaborative and resilient: You bring teams along, take feedback from engineers who are skeptical, share credit, and keep going when experiments fail or the tooling changes under you. You communicate clearly with engineers, managers and non-engineering partners.

You don't need all of these, but they're nice signals of fit:
Experience with coding agents at depth: skills, MCP servers, hooks, sub-agent orchestration, headless runs.
Built evaluation harnesses or benchmarks for coding agents, or LLM-as-judge grading tied to build and test outcomes.
Experience with sandboxed execution at scale: ephemeral dev environments, VM or container fleets, macOS build infrastructure.

title: Software Engineer II - Growth
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Software Engineer II, Growth
We are seeking a Software Engineer II for the Growth Marketing Engineering Team. You are the kind of engineer who gravitates toward the hardest problems at the intersection of technology and performance marketing: designing a low-latency bidding optimization engine, building a reliable creative generation pipeline, or defining the architectural patterns that will shape how Quince scales its growth stack. You operate with high autonomy, hold yourself to exceptional standards, and naturally raise the bar for the engineers around you through rigorous code reviews, sharp technical judgment, and a bias toward clean, durable solutions over quick fixes.
Responsibilities
Designing and implementing software features and components, following best practices and coding standards with minimal supervision.
Contributing to identifying the root cause of complex problems, scale, and stability challenges.
Proposing a solution to mitigate them in the short/medium/long term horizon.
Keeping up-to-date with new technologies, frameworks, and best practices in software development, and applying them to improve the performance and reliability of software systems.
Writing and maintaining technical documentation, API specifications, code documentation, and technical design documents.
Participating in code reviews and contributing to the development of coding standards and best practices.
Mentoring junior engineers and contributing to their professional growth and development.
Leading software development projects and working collaboratively with cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality software products
Qualifications
Required
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
At least 2 years of professional experience working in building user facing products.
Experience in advertisement performance tooling is a plus.
Proficient in using debugging tools and techniques.
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
Ability to work independently as well as part of a team.
Understand the hustle of a startup and are good with handling ambiguity.
Effectively communicate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Curious, quick learner, scrappy and someone who loves to experiment.
Pay Range: $188,000 - $203,000 + bonus + equity
WHY QUINCE?

High School/GED diploma required.
Demonstrated knowledge of mechanical operations.

title: Account Development Representative II
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
The Account Development Representative (ADR) job is the launching point for an individual looking for a successful career in SaaS sales. In this role, you will be at the front of Samsara’s go-to-market strategy. This includes hunting for leads, mapping enterprise accounts, and building demand for Samsara’s full line of products. This role is ideal for individuals looking to develop enterprise technology sales skills and to advance their careers. Successful ADRs earn accelerated commissions and head down the path for promotion into closing roles. You will work closely with top-tier executives and will see up close how sales organizations succeed.
This is a hybrid position open to candidates residing in Atlanta, Georgia and the Phoenix Metro Area of Arizona, requiring 3 days per week onsite and 2 days remote.
You should apply if :
You want to impact the industries that run our world : Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career : If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. Successful ADRs can see promotion to a closing role in two years or less.
You love talking to people : In this role you will average 50 calls to prospective customers daily.
You have innate curiosity in how businesses work : One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
You treat rejection as a learning experience : In this role, you will get hung up on and you will get told no. You need to have resilience to pick up the phone again and again to sell Samsara’s mission.
You want to be with the best : Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.
Minimum requirements for this role :
Ability and willingness to make 50 cold calls a day.
At least 6 months of sales experience and/or sales prospecting ability. This can be sales related coursework, sales competitions, etc.
Must be currently enrolled in an accredited 4-year Bachelor's degree program or within 1 year of graduation
An ideal candidate has :
Must demonstrate a growth mindset and a willingness to be collaborative with your teammates and in your selling process
6 Months experience with Salesforce, LI Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo.
Ability to quickly grasp technical concepts and embed AI usage into day to day operations

About the role:
Samsara's Customer Success team is on the front lines of business value delivery by helping customers adopt our platform, realize measurable business value, and renew and expand with confidence. Billing errors, concession requests, and cancellation or return exceptions currently land with CSMs, CS managers, and several partner teams, each holding part of the picture. As our customer base and billing complexity have grown, these cases take too long, repeat for the same reasons, and pull CSMs away from adoption and renewal work. As the Contract and Billing Resolution Specialist, you will be the single owner of complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts.
You will take a customer's report that something is wrong with their bill, work out what happened across systems and teams, choose the right path to fix it, and see it through, keeping the customer informed. It is part detective, part project manager, part customer advocate. You will also tell the teams who own the underlying systems and processes what keeps breaking.
Your role will be cross-functional, working alongside and connecting Customer Success Managers, Sales, Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal. This is a new role, and you will help shape the case record, the root-cause tags, and the monthly read-out that define how Customer Success resolves billing and contract cases at Samsara.
This is a remote  position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.
In this role, you will:
Own complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts, from the first report to a confirmed fix, and keep the customer informed in plain terms, including accounts that are delinquent or facing suspension.
Reconstruct the full story behind a billing error across contracts, order forms, segment or ownership changes, reprocessing, and invoicing, including cases with several AE handoffs and no clean record of what was promised.
Separate a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and choose the path that fixes the customer's billing, not only the immediate complaint.
Drive Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal to execute the fix.
Evaluate and prepare concession requests: confirm whether Samsara was at fault, size the request against policy and the approval matrix, write a short case summary (what happened, root cause, options considered and ruled out, recommendation, and risk), route it to the right approver, and confirm the credit is applied and the customer told.
Support cancellation, return, and ETF exceptions: validate eligibility (purchase and renewal dates, trial history, Return ACV, financing partner, documentation), prepare the case for the approving team, act as the Customer Success fallback when the first approver does not respond within the window, and make sure approved outcomes are processed.
Be the front door for billing, concession, and cancellation requests: log every request in a single case record, including those that arrive via Slack, email, or Gainsight; redirect them to the right path; and coach CSMs and AEs on what a complete request looks like.
Fix repeat causes: tag the root cause on every case, separate one-offs from systemic failures, and deliver a monthly read-out to the teams that own the systems and processes involved.
Carry forward the billing improvement work with Support, Finance, and Product, including earlier detection of billing problems that threaten renewals.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's operating principles, including Keep a High Bar, Be Intellectually Honest, and Solve Problems Together, as we scale.
Minimum requirements for the role:
4+ years of experience in billing operations, order to cash, revenue operations, deal desk, contracts, or a similar finance and operations role.
This is a demanding position with high internal visibility that requires strong priority management and high emotional intelligence.
Strong investigative skills: you can rebuild a timeline from incomplete or conflicting information across CRM, billing, and contract systems, including when the people involved have left.
Sound financial judgment about credits, concessions, reprocessing, and refunds, and a clear way of explaining your recommendation.
Customer-facing communication that stays honest and composed in hard conversations, and written summaries a leader can read once and decide on.
A record of driving results across teams without authority over them, including working to deadlines in an approval process.
Familiarity with order forms, amendments, and terms, and how they flow into billing.
Comfort with ambiguity and incomplete precedent, and rigorous case management so nothing drops across weeks and stakeholders.
Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues.
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience handling escalated or high-dollar billing disputes.
Experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, or an equivalent ERP, and CPQ tools. We also use Zendesk, Gainsight, and Sweethawk.
Customer Success, Support, or account management background with customer-facing financial or contract work.
Experience building or improving billing dispute processes.
Exposure to subscription or hardware-plus-subscription billing.
AI First: Experience using AI tooling to drive efficiency and outcomes.
Strong bias for action and insistence on high standards

About the role
AI is moving off the screen and into physical operations and Samsara is building it. If you want to be a product manager enabling the transformation behind how the real world works, join us.
We connect the vehicles, equipment, sites, and people behind the physical operations that power our economy. Our platform collects more than 30 trillion data points a year from vehicles that travel 99.9% of U.S. roads, and we design our own hardware to capture it. That mix of hardware, real-world data, and AI is why we're building things no one else can. We don't start with a model; we start with the data, embedded hardware, and deep customer understanding that make AI valuable.
And it's working. Samsara crossed $2.1 billion in ARR last quarter, growing 30% year over year, and we've been GAAP profitable for four straight quarters. Adoption of our AI agents has grown 7x since June, and voice agents overtook chat within four weeks of launch. We're just getting started.

We hire product managers into Samsara first and match you with the team and problem where you'll have the most impact. Problem spaces evolve consistently here and what's most important is your excitement about what and how Samsara is building.

You have strong commercial instincts and want to understand how the product gets sold.

title: Business Operations Generalist
description:
COMPANY BACKGROUND

Specter's mission is to help automate the physical world.

Today, we build video sensors with state-of-the-art AI agents that answer any question, anywhere in their environments. Our systems can automatically detect and reason about any physical activity captured on camera, from security incidents (e.g. perimeter intrusion, theft, LPR), to safety monitoring (e.g. PPE detection, injured people), to operational efficiency (e.g. material tracking, congestion monitoring). We offer both long range wireless (1km range) and wired sensor variants to suit any deployment.

Our co-founders Xerxes and Philip are passionate about empowering our partners in the fast approaching world of physical AI and robotics. We are a small, fast growing team who hail from Anduril, Tesla, Uber, and the U.S. Special Forces.




THE ROLE

We are looking for a Business Operations Generalist to join Specter's lean BizOps team. This person will work across deal support, pricing, market strategy, planning, finance, and company systems. Today the work leans more commercial, including working with our GTM teams on sales materials, customer value cases, and proposals. In a given week, it can mean a customer business case one day and a CRM cleanup the next. Some of it is strategic. Some of it is unglamorous. Part of the job is building the templates and systems that make that work repeatable, so the role will likely look different in 6 months, and may be less GTM oriented then. We want someone who enjoys that variety, jumps into new problems as they come up, owns the outcome, and leaves each process better than they found it. The right person is analytical, commercially sharp, highly organized, and comfortable working with leadership, sales, finance, product, and engineering in the same day.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - You will put together pricing, proposals, customer business cases, and value models for complex deals, and support contract review. Over time, you will turn this work into templates and systems the sales team can run on their own.

 - You will build business cases for new markets and new products, and keep the team current on what competitors are doing.

 - You will help leadership and the sales team see the pipeline clearly through forecasting, CRM hygiene, and dashboards.

 - You will support planning, budgeting, and board and investor reporting, and track spend across the business, including production, R&D, SaaS, and vendor spend.

 - You will build processes, documentation, and decision frameworks where today there may only be spreadsheets, Slack threads, and ad hoc decisions.

 - You will handle the day-to-day work that keeps the business running: cleaning up data, coordinating vendors, chasing down numbers, and taking problems from "someone should figure this out" to a clear owner and outcome.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3 to 5 years of experience in consulting, investment banking, or investing, or in business operations, revenue operations, or a similarly analytical role at an early-stage, high-growth startup.

 - Strong with spreadsheets and financial models, and comfortable in a CRM.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills.

 - Good judgment and the ability to prioritize when everything feels urgent.

 - A low-ego team player who takes on the detailed, behind-the-scenes work without being asked and improves it over time.

 - A builder mentality: you are excited to create the first version of a system and turn one-off work into something others can reuse.

 - A generalist who enjoys variety and is excited to take on whatever problem matters most, knowing the role will change as the company grows.

 - Comfortable working without much direction or full context. You find what you need, make a reasonable call, and flag what you assumed.

 - You use AI tools to improve systems and get more done, without handing your thinking to them.

 - Interest in physical AI, hard industries, critical infrastructure, defense, energy, or industrial technology and the ability and desire to get up to speed on technical products.

 - Based in San Francisco and excited to work in person.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Accountability

Ensure the technical and clinical vision defined at the start of the project is consistently understood and executed across all technical sub-teams, preventing scope creep or strategic drift.
Proactively identify and resolve friction between functional groups (e.g., Commercial timelines vs. R&D feasibility). You will serve as the primary mediator, fostering constructive debate to reach rapid, data-driven decisions without needing constant escalation.
Stage-Gate Governance & Strategic Execution
Lead the product team through formal Stage-Gate Reviews (Phase Exits). You must possess the executive presence to synthesize complex technical, clinical, and operational data into clear, actionable business narratives for the leadership team.
Proactively identify critical path risks. You will drive difficult trade-off decisions between scope, timeline, and resources, escalating structural blockers to the Executive Leadership Team only when necessary.
Collaborate with functional leadership to ensure appropriate resource allocation, ensuring the project aligns with the broader Tempus portfolio priorities.
Design Control & Operational Scale
Champion a development process compliant with Design Control (21 CFR 820) and ISO 13485 standards. You will guide the team through the rigors of LDT, 510(k), or PMA regulatory pathways.
Oversee the critical transition from R&D to Clinical Lab Operations. You will ensure the "order-to-result" workflow is robust, scalable, and ready for commercial volume prior to launch.
Act as the primary link between technical development and the Commercial organization, ensuring that technical milestones translate into market-ready value propositions.

Advanced degree (PhD, MD, MS) in Genetics, Molecular Biology, or Engineering required. MBA is a strong plus.
10+ years in the life sciences/diagnostics industry, with at least 4+ years serving as a Core Team Leader, Product Development Lead, or Program Director in a matrixed environment.
Deep experience in Oncology Diagnostics, NGS, or Liquid Biopsy is essential. Experience navigating FDA Class II/III medical device development (PMA/510k) is highly preferred.
Competencies
Expert knowledge of Phased-Gate/Stage-Gate development cycles. You understand the difference between tracking a timeline and leading a product to market.
High emotional intelligence and communication skills required to manage up to executive level  stakeholders. You act as the "single source of truth," filtering noise and delivering clarity.
Demonstrated ability to influence without authority. You can motivate and guide senior functional experts who do not report to you, maintaining momentum even when faced with organizational ambiguity.
Ability to "speak the language" of both the R&D scientists developing the chemistry and the Commercial leaders selling the test.
You don't just focus on the science; you focus on the manufacturability and operational scalability of the test.

Efficiency and success rate of Stage-Gate (Phase Exit) presentations to the Executive Committee.
Adherence to the roadmap timeline while ensuring Design Control compliance.
Seamless transfer to Operations with met KPIs for Turnaround Time (TAT) and success rates upon launch.
High engagement and clarity scores from cross-functional Core Team members, evidenced by reduced cross-departmental friction and unified project execution.
Why Join Us
At Tempus AI, we believe the future of medicine lies at the intersection of science and data. In this role, you will be at the center of that evolution, transforming how liquid biopsy and xF diagnostics provide clarity to clinicians and better outcomes for patients.
